title: t19325: fix(dispatch): size worker prelaunch lease to cover the canary bound (worker_ledger_ready_failed)
body:
## Task


Pulse workers lose their dispatch lease whenever the model canary runs a real probe for longer than about 110 seconds. The worker then exits with `worker_ledger_ready_failed`, the claim is released and the slot is wasted. Size the worker's prelaunch lease renewal to cover the bounded canary step, and extend the local dispatch-ledger lease at the same time.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Pulse workers lose their dispatch lease whenever the model canary runs a real probe for longer than about 110 seconds. The worker then exits with `worker_ledger_ready_failed`, the claim is released and the slot is wasted. Size the worker's prelaunch lease renewal to cover the bounded canary step, and extend the local dispatch-ledger lease at the same time.

## Why

Evidence (GH#40112 attempt `attempt:789867d0`, runner-local worker log):

- Dispatcher registered the ledger entry at 00:18:40Z with the default `PRELAUNCH_TTL=120` (`dispatch-ledger-helper.sh:62`), so it expired at 00:20:40Z.
- Worker renewed the GitHub claim at 00:18:40–00:18:49Z with `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_CLAIM_ORPHAN_GRACE:-120` (`headless-runtime-worker-ownership.sh:392`). That renewal does not touch `dispatch-ledger.jsonl`; `_dch_ledger_sync_transition` only updates the checkpoint ledger.
- Canary ran from 00:18:51Z to 00:21:24Z (153 s). `CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 180 (`headless-runtime-lib.sh:1383`), so the bound already exceeds both 120 s leases.
- `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh ready` at ~00:21:35Z hit `_lease_entry_is_active` = expired, giving `worker_ledger_ready_failed`. The GitHub `transition ready` would also have been denied (`dispatch-claim-helper.sh:1487`).
- Across 1,182 retained worker logs, the renewal-to-ready gap has a median of 7 s and a p90 of 13 s; only this attempt reached at least 120 s (165 s). It is rare, but it correlates with slow providers, so a provider slowdown would fail every cache-missing launch at once.

Manual dispatch already solved this: `_dsi_renew_prelaunch_lease` (`dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh:1342`) sizes its TTL from `_dsi_ready_timeout_seconds` (canary timeout + 60 s) plus a preparation allowance. Pulse workers do not.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-ownership.sh` `_hrw_renew_dispatch_prelaunch_lease`: compute the TTL as the larger of `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_CLAIM_ORPHAN_GRACE` (default 120) and `CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 180) + `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_PRELAUNCH_ALLOWANCE_SECONDS` (default 120). Pass it to `dispatch-claim-helper.sh transition prelaunch`, then make a best-effort ledger renewal with the same TTL.
2. `.agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`: add a `renew --session-key K --lease-token T [--lease-ttl N]` command. It only extends an active `prelaunch` lease for that token, never shortens it, and never turns a `ready` lease back into `prelaunch`.
3. The strict expiry checks on `ready` stay unchanged. Safety comes from sizing the lease, not from tolerating expiry.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-ownership.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- A worker whose canary takes up to `CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` keeps both its GitHub claim and its ledger lease active through the ready transition.
- `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh renew` extends an active prelaunch lease, is a no-op when the lease is already longer, and returns 1 for unknown or expired tokens and for leases in the `ready` phase.
- `shellcheck` is clean; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-atomic-lease.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-ledger-helper.sh` pass.

## Cost

A worker that dies during prelaunch now holds its dedup lease for up to 300 s instead of 120 s before it can be dispatched again. The GitHub claim already gives the same window.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

title: t19326: fix(recovery): external_trigger decisions re-poll at recheck_after or a bound...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19326` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(recovery): external_trigger decisions re-poll at recheck_after or a bounded default instead of parking forever

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Supervisor recovery decisions recorded with `wake=external_trigger` never expire on time. Holds waiting on something only polling can see (a website recovering, a ceremony date passing, a "recheck after" time) are therefore parked indefinitely, and the AI owner never looks again. Add an optional structured `recheck_after` to `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh record`, and give `external_trigger` decisions without one a bounded default re-poll interval. When either is due, the entry returns to the supervisor for re-assessment.

## Why

`_tbr_decision_active` (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh:114`) treats `external_trigger` like `human_decision`: it wakes only on a maintainer reply or a policy change. GH#39688 (t19249) added `external_trigger` so that settled holds stay out of the `/decisions` "Needs your decision" list, and it inherited the no-TTL rule from GH#38692. That rule is right for a pending human answer. It is wrong for events no GitHub signal will ever report.

Evidence from one runner's recovery store (2026-11-24, a managed product repo):

- 25 `external_trigger` decisions (median age 2.1 days, maximum 7.6 days). At least 13 have a time-bound `next_action`, for example "Recheck after 2026-11-23T15:12Z", "Recheck after 2026-11-23T10:51Z", "Recheck after 2026-11-24T16:00Z", "Keep holding until after the 30 November 2026 ceremony", "seven days of recorded 503 checks (on or after 2026-11-28)".
- Three of those rechecks fell due 9–14 hours earlier and nothing re-assessed them. Each one stays `status:blocked` until a person happens to reply.
- This is the "blocked is a label, not an instruction" gap. The AI owner wrote down when to look again, and the framework has nowhere to keep that.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` `tbr_record`: accept an optional `recheck_after` (ISO 8601 UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`), only with `wake=external_trigger`. Validate it with jq `fromdateiso8601` and store it as `recheck_after_epoch`. Reject an unknown key or a malformed or misplaced `recheck_after` with the existing error.
2. `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh` `_tbr_decision_active`: an `external_trigger` decision becomes inactive once `now >= recheck_after_epoch`, or, without one, once `recorded_epoch + BLOCKER_RECOVERY_EXTERNAL_TRIGGER_RECHECK` (new, default 259200, three days) has passed. `human_decision` keeps its positive-wake-only rule (GH#38692). Reply and policy-change wakes are unchanged.
3. `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md` step 6 and `.agents/reference/recovery-policy.md` step 5: document `recheck_after` and the default re-poll. Re-recording after a re-check sets the next `recheck_after`.

`/decisions` classification (`maintainer-decisions-helper.sh`) is unchanged; these holds still show as parked, not as questions.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`
- `.agents/reference/recovery-policy.md`

## Acceptance

- `record` accepts `{"wake":"external_trigger","next_action":...,"evidence":...,"recheck_after":"2026-11-25T16:00:00Z"}` and stores `recheck_after_epoch`. It rejects `recheck_after` on other wakes and rejects malformed values.
- `_tbr_decision_active` is active before `recheck_after` and inactive after it. Without `recheck_after`, it is inactive after the default interval. `human_decision` is still active past both.
- `shellcheck` is clean; `tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`, `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh` and `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh` pass.

## Cost

About 25 parked holds resurface roughly every three days (≈8 per day), against the 60+ per day that GH#38692 fixed. The decided-tier queue share from t19105 bounds the effect on undecided entries.

</details>

title: fix(issue-sync): enrich case 3 overwrites authored issue briefs (Files Scope lost on sentinel bodies)
body:
## What

`issue-sync-helper` enrich overwrote an authored worker-ready brief on #40112 (t19324) with a TODO-composed body, dropping `### Files Scope`, `## Acceptance` and `## Verification`. The dispatched worker had to restore the brief by hand before it could rely on the scope.

## Evidence

- #40112 body replaced at 2026-11-24T00:18:18Z by TODO sync. The task has no `todo/tasks/t19324-brief.md`, so `_enrich_update_issue` took **case 3** ("no brief + has sentinel → previously framework-synced, update on diff"), see `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-enrich.sh:313-394`.
- The authored brief lived only in the issue body. Because the body still carried the sync sentinel, any diff against the TODO-composed body counted as drift and was overwritten.

## Why

Case 3 assumes a sentinel body is fully framework-owned. An interactive author who expands a synced issue into a full brief (Files Scope, Acceptance, Verification) loses that content on the next sync, and workers then dispatch without a Files Scope or acceptance criteria.

When present, preserve the body (log `Preserving authored brief`) unless `--force`, or carry those sections into the composed body.

## Acceptance

- A sentinel-bearing issue body that contains `### Files Scope` not present in the TODO-composed body is not overwritten by enrich without `--force`.

title: t19327: perf(recovery): supervisor pending pass skips unchanged decided entries after...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19327` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

perf(recovery): supervisor pending pass skips unchanged decided entries after one issue read (3 of 131 entries observed per pass)

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the supervisor `pending` pass (and its `--count` trigger probe) skip decided queue entries that have not changed since their decision after one issue read, instead of reading comments and computing the brief revision for each one. Today a 45 s pass observes about 3 of 131 queued entries, so the LLM recovery supervisor rarely sees the holds that are actually due, and blocked issues wait days for an AI owner.

## Why

Evidence from one runner (2026-11-24, `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/terminal-blocker-recovery`; one managed product repo holds most entries):

- 131 queue entries; in the main repo 67 of 118 have a recorded decision.
- The latest trigger probe (`supervisor/last_blocker_recovery_probe.err`, 00:02Z) checked **3 entries** in its 45 s budget. One hit the 8 s stage cap (`incomplete stage=entry rc=124`), and the pass ended `incomplete stage=queue reason=unobserved_entries`.
- `gh-api-calls.log` for that probe shows 3–4 REST/GraphQL calls per entry (issue, comments, revision/timeline), about 0.6–2.6 s each through the wrapper, so 8–11 s per entry. The 45 s budget is fixed by the 120 s supervisor shell timeout (GH#35290), and the queue window is about 29 s of it.
- A recovery-policy edit (2026-11-23T04:17Z) woke 41 decided entries by design (t19068). About 21 h later only 6 had been re-assessed.
- `trigger=blocker_recovery` supervisor runs: 11-22 05:13, 09:54, 15:49; 11-23 17:02 (17 h after the previous cycle); 11-24 00:05. The probe only triggers a run when its small window happens to contain a due entry. Most windows contain only standing decided entries, which still cost the full 3–4 reads each before the decision check at the end of `_tbr_check_entry`.

For a decided entry whose decision is still active by time and policy, the only remaining wake is a reply newer than the decision, and any comment advances the issue's `updated_at`. Releases from a trusted retry, brief revision, dependency closure or permission window belong to the mechanical `rearm` pass (every `PULSE_BLOCKER_REARM_INTERVAL`, 600 s), which runs the same release code. Reading comments for an unchanged decided entry in the supervisor pass therefore cannot change its outcome.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` `_tbr_check_entry`: for the normal intake path (after `_tbr_check_intake_entry` returns 3), in non-rearm mode (supervisor `pending` and `--count`), right after the issue read: if a decision file exists, `_tbr_decision_active "$key"` (no comments, so only the time/TTL and policy checks) succeeds, and the issue `updated_at` is not later than the decision's `recorded_epoch` (compare as epoch via jq `fromdateiso8601`; a missing or unparsable value never skips), return 1 without the comments and revision reads. Log one stage line (`blocker-recovery: decided_unchanged repo=… issue=…`) for diagnosis.
2. Do not change the rearm pass, release logic, intake routing (`unclassified_hold`, `answered_hold`, `unexplained_hold`, `persistent_exclusion`, `policy_remote`), or the tier split in `terminal-blocker-recovery-pending.sh`.
3. `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md` "Terminal-blocker recovery": one sentence noting that the supervisor pass skips unchanged decided entries after the issue read, and that the rearm pass owns mechanical releases.

Reference pattern: `_tbr_skip_unchanged_entry` in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh` (the rearm-mode equivalent keyed on `rearm_checked_updated_at`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`

## Acceptance

- A decided entry with an active decision and `updated_at` not after `recorded_epoch` is skipped after one issue read in `pending` and `pending --count`. It is still fully checked when `updated_at` is newer, when the decision is time-due or policy-changed, or in rearm mode.
- Runtime: with `AIDEVOPS_BLOCKER_RECOVERY_DIR` pointing to a copy of a real recovery store, `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending --count` observes at least 3x more entries per 45 s call than before (compare `checking stage=entry_issue` counts on stderr). The copy must not be the live store, because `pending` moves cursors.
- `shellcheck -x` clean; `tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`, `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh`, `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh` and `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` pass.

## Not in scope

Running the synchronous LLM supervisor outside the pulse instance lock (GH#40112 / t19324 covers dispatch during maintenance stages) and batching issue reads per repository. File a follow-up if the 3x target is missed.

title: t19328: fix(recovery): blocked worker checkpoints lose their AI owner when the hold is released without a rearm receipt (GH#39971 idle 18h)
body:
## What

A worker's blocked draft checkpoint can be left with no AI owner. Something removes `needs-ai-recovery` and `status:blocked` from the issue without posting a `terminal-blocker-rearmed` receipt. The t19115 auto-continue route then never qualifies, `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` blocks ordinary dispatch, and only a human approval or a closed draft can move the issue again. Find the component that releases the hold without a receipt and fix it: either post a qualifying receipt or keep the hold. Also make a fix to the blocking target code landing on the default branch count as `revision_changed` for `target_code_blocker` checkpoints, so the draft continues without a person.

## Why

Evidence: GH#39971 / draft PR #39984 (marcusquinn/aidevops). All times are 2026-11-23Z unless stated.

- 08:17. Worker (runner `vladimirdulov`) finished the scoped fix and verified it (35/35, five runs under load). It released `reason=blocked`, class `target_code_blocker`, because an unrelated test failed in the full-suite validator: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-runtime-events.mjs` "queued sqliteExec writes land on normal process exit", 21|20. Labels became `status:blocked` and `needs-ai-recovery`. The terminal-blocker comment said "Owner: the recovery supervisor (no human action)".
- 09:56 / 10:33 / 11:28. `status:blocked` was removed, re-added, then removed again, and at 11:29 `needs-ai-recovery` was removed, all by the same runner. **No `terminal-blocker-rearmed` receipt or decision comment was posted.**
- 11:31. Another runner posted `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION`, asking the brief owner (a human with write access) to approve or close the draft.
- 16:01. `status:available` was added by the same runner. Dispatch then logged `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` / `worker_draft_checkpoint_cooldown` every cycle.
- 17:49. GH#40021 fixed the blocking test on main. Nothing re-armed the checkpoint.
- 2026-11-24 ~02:35. A maintainer session confirmed the test passes 3/3 on main and published the approval by hand, after the draft had been idle 18 h.

`checkpoint_policy` is enabled for marcusquinn/aidevops, and `auto_continue_rearmed` defaults on, so with a receipt this would have continued automatically (`.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md` "Re-armed blocked checkpoints (t19115)"). Comparable cases: one private managed product repository has 4 open `origin:worker` drafts idle over 24 h on 2026-11-24 (not yet classified).

## How

1. Trace which code path removes `needs-ai-recovery` / `status:blocked` from an issue without writing a receipt. Candidates:
   - `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh` (`_tbr_release_decided_hold` and its label projection)
   - `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (`_tbr_check_entry`, rearm decision near lines 870–934)
   - `.agents/scripts/pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh`
   - stale-blocked / label-normalisation sweeps (`rg -n "needs-ai-recovery" .agents/scripts`)
   - the LLM supervisor decision path (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`, supervisor guidance near line 513)

   Use the 11:28–11:29 label events. The removing runner's `pulse.log` is not available here, so reason from the code paths that unlabel both labels together.
2. Fix it so any release of a terminal-blocker hold on an issue with an open blocked worker draft either posts the qualifying receipt (`revision_changed` / `trusted_retry`) or leaves the hold and the recovery queue entry in place.
3. For `target_code_blocker`, confirm that `terminal_blocker_task_revision` changes when the default branch advances past a fix to the blocking file, so the rearm yields `revision_changed`. If its inputs do not cover the failing file named in the release, record the blocking test/file path in the observation and include it in the revision.

Touch `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` only if step 3 needs new revision inputs, and `pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh` only if it is the unlabeling path. The reference doc change is one sentence on the guarantee.

Reference patterns: `_tbr_rearm_reason_line` and receipts in `terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh`; `pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh` lines 40–80 (how t19115 consumes receipts).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-lifecycle.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh`
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`

## Acceptance

- The unlabeling path is named, with file:line, in the PR body.
- With the fix, an issue released `blocked` / `target_code_blocker` with an open worker draft never ends up `status:available` with neither a receipt nor `needs-ai-recovery`.
- A fix landing on the default branch for the blocking file produces a `terminal-blocker-rearmed reason=revision_changed` receipt, and with `checkpoint_policy` on the draft is auto-approved through the existing `dispatch-approved` gates. Verify with the existing suites `tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh`, `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh` and `tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`, extending a fixture only if no existing case covers the path.
- `shellcheck -x` clean on touched scripts.

## Not in scope

Enabling `checkpoint_policy` for other repositories (operator decision), or changing the human-approval route for decision-class blockers.

title: perf(recovery): improve pending throughput when decided skip windows miss the 3x target
body:
## Outcome

Improve supervisor recovery queue throughput when unchanged-decision skipping does not meet the 3x target. Follow-up explicitly requested by #40126; implementation checkpoint PR #40128.

## Evidence

Two 45-second `pending --count` runs on independent copies of the same real 81-entry recovery store observed 9 issue reads before the change and 6 after; neither window encountered an eligible unchanged decision (zero `decided_unchanged` lines). Both exhausted the bounded pass with exit 2. This does not establish a code regression or the intended 3x gain: queue mix and upstream latency still dominate. Ten isolated entry-path runtime cases passed, including unchanged/equal timestamps, newer/malformed/missing timestamps, rearm, due TTL/external rechecks, changed policy and invalid records.

## Implementation

Profile the bounded pass on a copied store, classify eligible decisions and slow stages using aggregate counts only, then implement the smallest additional throughput improvement supported by evidence. Reuse `_tbr_skip_decided_unchanged` and existing queue tier/cursor discipline. Do not extend permissions, weaken trust/release guards, change intake semantics or modify live recovery state during profiling. Batch reads are a possible approach, not a prescribed solution. Target paths may require a brief correction after profiling; persist it before edits.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-pending.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-github.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`

## Verification and acceptance

- Run baseline and candidate `pending --count` against identical independent copied stores, with 45-second budgets and matching initial cursors; report `checking stage=entry_issue` counts and eligible skip counts, without private repository names or content.
- Establish a representative decided-entry window and achieve at least 3x baseline observations, or implement a measured alternative with explicitly quantified limitations.
- Preserve tier fairness, fail-closed partial reads, trusted-comment restrictions, and mechanical rearm behavior.
- Run `shellcheck -x` on changed scripts plus `.agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`, `test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh`, `test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh` and `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`.

title: fix(recovery): jq compile error in terminal_blocker_fetch_issue_batch breaks batched queue reads
body:
## Summary

`terminal_blocker_fetch_issue_batch()` in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-github.sh` (added by merged PR #40133, GH#40131) has a jq compile error, so the supervisor's batched queue read never succeeds. Every `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` run logs `incomplete stage=issue_batch rc=1` and falls back to per-entry reads. That fallback uses the stage budget the batch was meant to save, so the queue ends `budget_exhausted` / `unobserved_entries` (seen on the 2026-11-24 06:22Z supervisor pulse).

## Evidence

Observed output from `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending`:

```
blocker-recovery: checking stage=issue_batch
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected '+', expecting '}' (Unix shell quoting issues?) at <top-level>, line 6:
		[.[] | {key:(.nameWithOwner | ascii_downcase | sub("/"; "--")) + "--" + (.i.number | tostring),
jq: 1 compile error
blocker-recovery: incomplete stage=issue_batch rc=1
```

Cause: jq object-construction values must be one term. `{key:(A) + "--" + (B)}` is invalid. The whole value needs its own parentheses. The faulty line is still present on `main` (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-github.sh:25`).

## Fix

File: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-github.sh:25`

```jq
[.[] | {key:((.nameWithOwner | ascii_downcase | sub("/"; "--")) + "--" + (.i.number | tostring)),
```

I checked the corrected expression locally:

```
jq -nc '[{nameWithOwner:"A/b",i:{number:1}}] | [.[] | {key:((.nameWithOwner | ascii_downcase | sub("/"; "--")) + "--" + (.i.number | tostring)), value:1}] | from_entries'
# => {"a--b--1":1}
```

The key matches what `terminal_blocker_fetch_queue_issue()` looks up (`${repo//\//--}--${issue}`, lowercased).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-github.sh`
- Run `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` from a supervisor workspace. It should no longer print `incomplete stage=issue_batch rc=1` or the jq compile error.
- Optional: grep other jq programs added in #40133 for the same unparenthesised `{key:(x) + ...}` pattern.

title: t19330: perf(pulse): defer same-tier dispatch candidates for a short TTL after a no-selectable-model canary failure
body:
## Task


When a worker model tier has just proven unselectable (canary rc 75/78), skip further dispatch candidates **for that same tier** for a short TTL *before* they run the ~31 s pre-dispatch gate ceremony, instead of rediscovering "no selectable model" at the canary on every candidate.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When a worker model tier has just proven unselectable (canary rc 75/78), skip further dispatch candidates **for that same tier** for a short TTL *before* they run the ~31 s pre-dispatch gate ceremony, instead of rediscovering "no selectable model" at the canary on every candidate.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-24 03:00–08:00Z on one runner (dispatch-stages.tsv + pulse.log): 725 dispatch ceremonies, 721 ended at `pre_runtime_failure:canary_preflight` with `no selectable model in tier standard|thinking`. Each spent ~31 s in GitHub-API-heavy gates first (one sampled candidate: `dedup.dedup_check` 16.7 s, `predispatch_validator` 2.8 s, `eligibility_gate` 2.5 s, `prebootstrap_gates` 2.3 s, `ceremony_total` 36.2 s) before `resolve_tier_model` (0.7 s) and `canary_preflight` (4.7 s) returned 75. That is hours of dispatch time and thousands of GitHub calls per outage window, while candidates in still-selectable tiers (e.g. `tier:simple` → `openai/gpt-6-luna`) waited behind them. Any install whose tier depends on one OAuth provider hits this every time that pool is exhausted (thinking tier here: `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` only, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` is ChatGPT-OAuth-denied). Root-cause diagnostics shipped in GH#40140; this task removes the wasted ceremony.

## How

- Write a tier-keyed marker in the rc 75/78 branch of `_dlw_canary_preflight` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`): tier name, epoch, and the `tier_selection_unavailable ...` reasons line it already extracts (GH#40140). Store it next to the existing pulse state (follow the TTL negative-cache pattern in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-canary.sh` `_canary_negative_cache_is_active`, `CANARY_NEGATIVE_TTL_SECONDS` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`). Clear the marker when a canary for that tier passes.
- In `dispatch_with_dedup` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`), immediately after `_dispatch_load_and_validate_metadata` and before `_dispatch_dedup_check_layers`, resolve the would-be dispatch tier **without** calling `headless-runtime-helper.sh select` (labels via `_resolve_worker_tier` / `_dlw_has_explicit_tier_label`, bundle tier via `_dlw_bundle_model_tier`, and the explicit `model_override` case — see `_dlw_resolve_tier_and_model` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-model.sh`; factor a tier-only helper rather than duplicating logic). If a fresh marker (default TTL 120 s, env `PULSE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE_TTL_SECONDS`) exists for that tier, log one line `[dispatch_with_dedup] Deferring #N in slug — tier T unavailable (cached Ns ago) [reasons]` and return the same rc the canary path returns today, with no claim, comment, fast-fail, backoff, or worktree written.
- An explicit `model_override` naming a concrete model must still be allowed through when its provider differs from every provider in the cached reasons (pins are not tier selection).

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-model.sh

- After one candidate in tier T fails the canary with rc 75, the next candidate in tier T within the TTL is deferred before `dedup.dedup_check` runs (no `dedup.*` stage rows for it in dispatch-stages.tsv), and logs the cached reasons.

title: Make Tabby authentication contention tests deterministic
body:
## Outcome

Make the existing Tabby authentication contention tests establish that competing acquisition attempts actually occur before asserting serialization. Keep production authentication behavior unchanged and use the current unittest runner only.

## Evidence and scope

CodeRabbit's exact-head review of PR #37733 at `397078a9480130e0dbdec7e3a82095113f5aee86` identified a non-blocking test-quality nit in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-sessions.py`, around lines 536 and 567. Inspection confirms the first test sets `started` before entering `authentication_slot`, then waits 50 ms to infer contention; the 20-worker test uses a 5 ms wait. Unusual scheduling can therefore weaken the assertions without showing a production runtime defect. The existing 70-test suite and operator desktop acceptance (21/21 sessions connected, repeated restore deduplicated) passed at that head.

This is additive deterministic-test hardening, not a blocker for the accepted runtime behavior in PR #37733. Do not expand into production refactoring or new test infrastructure.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-sessions.py`

Target the methods `AuthenticationTests.test_next_handshake_waits_only_until_authenticated_not_session_exit` and `AuthenticationTests.test_twenty_tabs_keep_one_handshake_pending_while_sessions_remain_live`.

Read-only reference: `.agents/scripts/tabby_session_auth.py` and the existing `TransportTests` marker-release assertions in the same test file.

## How

1. Inspect the current merged versions of the named tests; preserve newer unrelated changes.
2. Synchronize on actual attempted lock acquisition rather than the earlier worker-start signal. Use bounded events/barriers and existing mocking primitives; avoid timing-only readiness assumptions and scheduler-speed requirements.
3. Retain checks that only one handshake is pending and the next handshake proceeds after authentication acknowledgment while connected sessions remain alive.
4. Demonstrate through a temporary local mutation that disabling authentication locking makes the relevant assertions fail. Restore the production implementation before committing; do not add a test-only production switch or commit the mutation.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-session-helper.sh` passes normally and on repeated runs.
- Record the focused mutation-check failure and verify production files are unchanged afterward.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main` and `git diff --check` pass.
- No new runner, dependency, fixtures, CI gate, desktop sessions or remote SSH access is required.

## Tier and discovery

Standard: the write surface and behavior are decided, but event coordination requires semantic implementation choices. A prework discovery pass found the original PR and no duplicate open task for deterministic Tabby contention checks. This is a test-only, reversible follow-up; no seeded draft PR is needed.

## Related

Ref #37733

title: t19331: fix(setup): source-access broker guard freezes every deploy when the active runtime already differs from the broker
body:
## Task


Narrow the source-access broker deploy guard (`_runtime_bundle_check_source_access_broker`, `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy-bundle.sh`) so it refuses a runtime deployment only when the **active** runtime currently matches the installed broker. That is the only case where a working source-access read flow exists to preserve. When the active runtime already differs from the broker, deploy and print a warning that names `aidevops setup --scope source-access` as the reconcile step. Today the guard refuses unconditionally.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Narrow the source-access broker deploy guard (`_runtime_bundle_check_source_access_broker`, `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy-bundle.sh`) so it refuses a runtime deployment only when the **active** runtime currently matches the installed broker. That is the only case where a working source-access read flow exists to preserve. When the active runtime already differs from the broker, deploy and print a warning that names `aidevops setup --scope source-access` as the reconcile step. Today the guard refuses unconditionally.

## Why

The guard shipped in PR #35518 (merged 2026-11-24 08:02Z). From 08:31Z, every `aidevops-auto-update` run on a maintainer runner has failed in `deploy_aidevops_agents` with exit 1 and the error `Refusing incompatible source-access runtime deployment: source-access-helper.py differs from the installed broker` (8 consecutive failures by 10:07Z in `~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log`). No merged fix reaches the Pulse/worker runtime, including dispatch fixes merged the same day.

Evidence that nothing is preserved: the plugin's broker check `sourceAccessBrokerMatches` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/source-access-approval.mjs`) requires sha256 equality between the broker and the deployed runtime helper/core. On the affected runner the deployed runtime helper (deployed before the guard existed) already differs from the root-owned broker (installed 2026-11-06, before helper change GH#39049 on 2026-11-18). So source-access approvals already fail closed, and refusing deployment only freezes everything else until someone runs a sudo ceremony.

The guard's own comment states its purpose: "Preserve an installed broker's working read flow instead of activating newer helpers that its byte-for-byte runtime check will reject". When no working flow exists, refusal serves no purpose.

## How

- Extract the existing per-file comparison loop into a helper that reports the first mismatching name (helper, core, optional documents module, plus the symlink/partial-broker fail-closed cases).
- `_runtime_bundle_check_source_access_broker`: accept an optional third argument, the active target dir. Keep the current refusal when no active root is given (existing tests), or when the active root's files all match the broker. Otherwise print a warning and return 0. This is not a trust grant: the broker stays unchanged, and the plugin's sha256 check keeps approvals fail-closed until reconciliation.
- Pass `target_dir` at both call sites: `_runtime_bundle_stage` (line ~472) and `_runtime_bundle_activate_locked` (line ~696).

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy-bundle.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-atomic-runtime-bundle-deploy.sh

## Acceptance

- Active runtime matches broker and candidate differs: refused (existing protection retained).
- Active runtime already differs from broker and candidate differs: deploys with a warning naming `aidevops setup --scope source-access`.
- No active root passed: behaviour unchanged (all existing `test_source_access_broker_compatibility` assertions pass).
- ShellCheck clean; `test-atomic-runtime-bundle-deploy.sh` passes.

## Verification

Extend `test_source_access_broker_compatibility` with the two active-root cases (cheap; existing fixtures). After merge, the next auto-update `deploy_aidevops_agents` row in `setup-stage-timings.log` exits 0 and `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh` contains `_dlw_tier_unavailable_defers_candidate`.

## Task Brief

## What

Make `cleanup_legacy_aidevops_temp_artifacts` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`) cost a bounded, near-constant number of processes per setup run, and stop the main producers leaking per-process temp entries into the macOS per-user temp root.

## Why

On a maintainer runner the stage took 52–761 s on each of the last 10 setup runs (`~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log`, 2026-11-23/24; 761 s at 10:03Z). The macOS temp root (`getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR`) held ~7,700 `aidevops-*` entries. The loop forks two `stat` processes for every pattern match (owner via `stat`, mtime via `_file_mtime_epoch`) before the 7-day age test. Almost all entries are younger than 7 days, so they are rescanned on every run. That is about 10,000 forks per setup under worker load, on every auto-update.

Largest leakers by count (point-in-time sample):

- 1,904 `aidevops-pulse-pr-list-provider-*` (~194 created in the last 24 h): per-PID dirs from `.agents/scripts/pulse-pr-list-cache.sh` (`${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/aidevops-pulse-pr-list-provider-${$}`) and `pulse-wrapper.sh` (`…-provider-cache-${$}`).
- 1,036 `aidevops-gh-response.*` and 1,036 `aidevops-gh-secondary.*`: `mktemp -t` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (around lines 675–708).
- 1,012 `aidevops-pulse-allow-auto-merge-*`: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` (around line 1583).

## How

1. In `cleanup_legacy_aidevops_temp_artifacts`, replace the per-candidate glob loop with one `find "$root" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -type l -user "$uid" \( -name 'aidevops-update-*' -o … \) -mtime +N -print0`, where N is derived from `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`. Convert to minutes with `-mmin +M` so the existing 60-second test override still works.
   - Keep the per-entry `_legacy_temp_artifact_is_active` PID check and `rm -rf` only for the (few) stale matches.
   - Keep the `/var/folders/*/T` root guard and the existing pattern list.
   - Bash 3.2: read with `while IFS= read -r -d '' candidate`.
2. At the producers, remove the per-process entry on exit, or create it under the managed workspace (`${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`, which already has age-based cleanup), whichever is smaller per file.
   - Follow the existing `trap … EXIT` cleanup patterns in each script.
   - If a producer's lifecycle makes this non-trivial, leave it and say so in the PR. Step 1 alone removes the setup cost.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-managed-temp-workspace.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-pr-list-cache.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
- .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh

## Acceptance

- `test-managed-temp-workspace.sh` passes unchanged (legacy cleanup semantics: owner-only, no symlinks, age-gated, active-PID entries kept).
- With ~5,000 young matching entries, the cleanup spawns O(1) processes beyond the stale matches. Run `time` on a fixture of a few thousand fresh files: well under 5 s.
- ShellCheck clean; Bash 3.2 parse passes (pre-commit ratchet).

## Verification

Run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-managed-temp-workspace.sh`. Then time the function against a temp fixture of ~3,000 fresh `aidevops-gh-response.*` files, setting `AIDEVOPS_LEGACY_TEMP_ROOT` to the fixture dir, before and after the change. After deploy, check that the `cleanup_legacy_aidevops_temp_artifacts` rows in `setup-stage-timings.log` drop to single-digit seconds.

</details>

Stop `aidevops-auto-update` from following a deterministic deploy refusal in the incremental `setup.sh --stage ai-session` with a full `setup.sh --non-interactive` run that is certain to fail the same way. Record and surface the refusal reason instead.

## Why

`_run_setup_ai_session_with_fallback` (`.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper-check.sh`, ~line 251) retries a full setup after any ai-session failure. On 2026-11-24, the source-access broker guard refused every `deploy_aidevops_agents` (fixed for the drifted-runtime case in GH#40147). Each auto-update cycle then ran the ai-session stage and a full setup, and both failed in the same guard. There were 8 consecutive `deploy_aidevops_agents` exit-1 rows between 08:31Z and 10:07Z. The only trace was in `auto-update.log`; nothing told the user why merged fixes were not reaching the runtime.

Candidates: the source-access broker refusal in `_runtime_bundle_check_source_access_broker` and the stale-candidate refusal in `_runtime_bundle_activate_locked` (both in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy-bundle.sh`).

- In `_run_setup_ai_session_with_fallback`, skip the full-setup fallback for that exit code. Record `update_state "update" "$remote" "deploy_refused"`, together with the refusal line from the log tail, so `aidevops status` / `auto-update-helper-status.sh` can show it.

title: t19334: perf(setup): skip per-repo guard hook reinstall when the installed hook fingerprint is current
body:
## Task


Make the five per-repo hook-rollout stages in non-interactive setup cost near-zero when nothing changed. The stages are `setup_privacy_guard`, `setup_complexity_guard`, `setup_repo_verify_guard`, `setup_canonical_guard` and `setup_task_id_guard`. Today each one re-runs a full installer subprocess for every registered repo on every setup.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the five per-repo hook-rollout stages in non-interactive setup cost near-zero when nothing changed. The stages are `setup_privacy_guard`, `setup_complexity_guard`, `setup_repo_verify_guard`, `setup_canonical_guard` and `setup_task_id_guard`. Today each one re-runs a full installer subprocess for every registered repo on every setup.

## Why

Merged fixes reach the runtime only after `setup.sh --stage ai-session` / `--non-interactive` finishes. In the 24 h to 2026-11-24T11Z, `~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log` showed these average durations: privacy 160 s (max 341), complexity 117 s (max 307), repo-verify 150 s (max 400), canonical 189 s (max 706), task-id 106 s (max 354). That is about 720 s of every setup run. Concurrent setups also queue behind the lock for up to 900 s and then fail with exit 75. On 2026-11-24 an `aidevops update` timed out at 900 s behind an auto-update run that was spending 332 s in `setup_privacy_guard` alone.

Cause: each guard loops `jq -r '.initialized_repos[].path'` (101 repos on this runner) and runs `bash install-pre-push-guards.sh install --guard <g>` (909 lines, sources libs, runs several `git rev-parse`/`git config` calls) or the equivalent canonical/task-id installer per repo. That is about 500 bash processes per setup, even when every hook is already current.

## How

- Add a cheap per-repo up-to-date check before each installer subprocess, and skip the subprocess when it passes. Suggested design (the worker may choose an equivalent):
  - Compute one fingerprint per guard per setup run: a sha256 over the installer script, its sourced libs (e.g. `git-hooks-path-lib.sh`) and the hook template/source files it writes.
  - Write the fingerprint into the managed hook header when installing (e.g. a `# aidevops-guard-fingerprint: <sha>` line). Some hooks may already carry a managed marker; reuse it if so.
  - Fast path per repo: resolve the hooks dir without spawning the installer, then read the managed hook's header. If the fingerprint matches, count the repo as `ok` (or `current`) and continue. This must stay correct when `core.hooksPath` is set (Beads): fall back to the installer whenever the hooks path cannot be resolved cheaply or confidently.
  - Mismatch, missing hook, unmanaged hook or any doubt → run the existing installer unchanged. Correctness must not regress.
- Optionally, fold the privacy and complexity loops (same installer, `--guard privacy` / `--guard complexity`) into a single pass per repo if the installer already accepts multiple guards.
- Keep the existing summary lines (`Privacy guard: ok=… conflict=… skip=… err=…`) and add a `current=` count, so the log shows how many repos took the fast path.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/guard-rollout-cache-lib.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-guard-rollout-cache.sh

Brief repaired: add a shared conservative fingerprint/receipt library used by all five rollout callers and three installers, plus focused regression and 100-repo timing coverage. This avoids duplicated cache logic and verifies effective hooksPath, changed inputs, deleted/unmanaged/modified hooks and unchanged-run performance. Verify with bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-guard-rollout-cache.sh and existing installer suites plus ShellCheck. No hard boundaries or authority changes.

- .agents/scripts/setup/_privacy_guard.sh
- .agents/scripts/setup/_complexity_guard.sh
- .agents/scripts/setup/_repo_verify_guard.sh
- .agents/scripts/setup/_canonical_guard.sh
- .agents/scripts/setup/_task_id_guard.sh
- .agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh
- .agents/scripts/install-canonical-guard.sh
- .agents/scripts/install-task-id-guard.sh

## Acceptance

- When no installer or template changed, a second consecutive setup spends ≤10 s total across the five guard stages on a 100-repo registry (measure with `setup-stage-timings.log`).
- A changed installer or template, a deleted hook, or an unmanaged hook still takes the installer path and produces the same outcome as today.
- `core.hooksPath` repos still get hooks in the effective hooks dir.
- Existing guard installer tests pass (`rg -l 'install-pre-push-guards|install-canonical-guard|install-task-id-guard' .agents/scripts/tests/`); ShellCheck clean; shell rules (`local var="$1"`, explicit returns) hold.

## Verification

Run `setup.sh --non-interactive` twice and compare the five stage durations in `~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log`. Then touch one installer, rerun, and confirm every repo is reinstalled. Delete one repo's managed pre-push hook and confirm only that repo is reinstalled.

title: t19335: fix(update): hand off to an in-flight newer setup on lock timeout instead of reporting a false deploy failure
body:
## Task


When `aidevops update` times out waiting for the setup lock (setup exit 75), check whether the current lock owner started after the canonical checkout reached the target SHA. If it did, that owner will deploy the same code. Wait for it (bounded), then verify convergence, instead of failing with `Agent deployment failed: setup exited with code 75`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When `aidevops update` times out waiting for the setup lock (setup exit 75), check whether the current lock owner started after the canonical checkout reached the target SHA. If it did, that owner will deploy the same code. Wait for it (bounded), then verify convergence, instead of failing with `Agent deployment failed: setup exited with code 75`.

## Why

On 2026-11-24 the PR #40149 fix was merged at 10:53Z and `aidevops update` was run at 10:55Z. It waited 900 s behind the auto-update's ai-session run (pid 40171). Then the auto-update's full-setup fallback (pid 31452, started 11:09Z, after the fast-forward) took the lock before the waiter did, and `aidevops update` exited 1 with "Agent deployment failed". The deploy was already in flight with the fixed code. The CLI reported a false failure after 15 minutes, and the operator or session had no supported way to wait for the real outcome. Whoever runs `aidevops update` right after a merge hits this whenever auto-update is mid-run.

## How

- In `_run_update_setup_transaction` (`aidevops.sh`, ~line 284), handle `setup_exit == 75` separately from other failures:
  - Read the lock owner from `${AIDEVOPS_SETUP_LOCK_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/locks/setup-noninteractive.lock.d}`: `owner.pid`, `started_at_epoch`, `command`.
  - Capture an epoch just after the canonical fast-forward or up-to-date check in the update flow, before setup runs. If the owner's `started_at_epoch` is later and its command is a deploying setup (`--stage ai-session` or `--non-interactive`), print an info line saying deployment was handed off to in-flight setup pid N.
  - Poll `kill -0` on that pid, bounded by a new `AIDEVOPS_UPDATE_HANDOFF_WAIT_S` (default ≈1800). Then run `_update_verify_deployment_state "$expected_sha"`. Return 0 if it converged; otherwise print a precise error naming the pid and the timings log.
  - If the owner started before the fast-forward, keep today's failure behaviour; that owner runs older code.
- Reuse the existing lock-owner readers in `setup.sh` (~lines 920–1018) where they can be sourced safely, or duplicate them minimally. Edit `setup.sh` only to extract a shared lock-owner reader.

### Files Scope

- aidevops.sh
- setup.sh

## Acceptance

- Lock timeout with an owner started after the fast-forward: `aidevops update` waits for that owner and exits 0 if `.deployed-sha` converges to the expected SHA. It exits non-zero with a clear message if it does not.
- Lock timeout with an older owner: unchanged failure.
- Exit codes other than 75: unchanged.
- ShellCheck clean; `local var="$1"`; explicit returns.

## Verification

Simulate with a fake lock dir (`AIDEVOPS_SETUP_LOCK_DIR` pointing to a temp dir) whose owner is a `sleep` process with `started_at_epoch` after the captured epoch. Stub setup to exit 75 and stub `_update_verify_deployment_state` to return 0. Confirm `aidevops update` returns 0 after the sleep ends. Repeat with an older `started_at_epoch` and confirm it still fails.

</details>

title: t19336: fix(watchdog): extend the elapsed hard-kill cap once for workers whose session DB proves live tool progress
body:
## Task


Stop the worker activity watchdog from hard-killing workers at the 1500 s elapsed cap while their isolated OpenCode DB proves live tool progress (`tool_output_active`). Add one bounded extension (a separate, longer absolute cap) for DB-proven activity. Keep a hard backstop and keep today's behaviour for every other liveness class.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop the worker activity watchdog from hard-killing workers at the 1500 s elapsed cap while their isolated OpenCode DB proves live tool progress (`tool_output_active`). Add one bounded extension (a separate, longer absolute cap) for DB-proven activity. Keep a hard backstop and keep today's behaviour for every other liveness class.

## Why

`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-dispatch.log` records 179 `worker_killed reason=hard_kill_cap_active` events from 2026-10-21 to 2026-11-24, classified by `cap_liveness`:

| cap_liveness | kills |
|---|---|
| tool_output_active | 102 (57%) |
| ci_wait | 38 |
| cpu_active | 24 |
| network_active | 13 |
| none_observed | 2 |

On 2026-11-23..24 alone there were 25 kills, 15 of them `tool_output_active`.

`worker-activity-helper.sh summary` (24 h to 2026-11-24T11:27Z) shows `watchdog_stall_killed` as the largest non-success class by slot time: 23 runs, 13.5 slot-hours, 7.3% of all worker slot time. That is more than `blocked` (12.1 h). Each kill also costs a redispatch ceremony (spawned ceremonies average 266 s in `dispatch-stages.tsv`) and the session's accumulated context. The t19266 pre-kill WIP push preserves only committed work.

Mechanism (`.agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh`):

- `_monitor` resets the stall counter only on output-file growth.
- Once stdout has been quiet for `STALL_TIMEOUT` (600 s), `_monitor_handle_confirmed_stall` calls `_monitor_enforce_hard_kill` first (~line 920).
- `_monitor_enforce_hard_kill` kills whenever total elapsed ≥ `HARD_KILL_SECONDS` (`WORKER_STALL_HARD_KILL_SECONDS`, default 1500). Its liveness sample (~lines 877–897) only labels the kill.
- GH#39197 (`_watchdog_db_part_activity`) already defers ordinary stalls when DB `part.time_updated` is fresh, but the cap check runs before that deferral.

## How

- Add `WORKER_STALL_HARD_KILL_ACTIVE_SECONDS`, default 3000 and clamped to ≥ `HARD_KILL_SECONDS`; `0` means "same as HARD_KILL_SECONDS".
- In `_monitor_enforce_hard_kill`, when elapsed ≥ `HARD_KILL_SECONDS` but < the active cap, and `_watchdog_db_part_activity` succeeds:
  - Emit a `[lifecycle] worker_cap_extended ... cap_liveness=tool_output_active elapsed=… active_cap=…` event to the lifecycle log and the `.watchdog_events` sidecar, using the existing deferral event writer.
  - Return 0 (continue monitoring) instead of killing.
  - At or beyond the active cap, kill exactly as today with `reason=hard_kill_cap_active`.
- Optional, only if trivially safe: treat `ci_wait` the same way. Leave `cpu_active`, `network_active` and `none_observed` unchanged; those signals are weaker evidence of task advancement (see the GH#34068 caution).
- Report the effective active cap in `activity_watchdog_started` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh` ~line 435) and in `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` "Quiet worker not killed (GH#36700)", so external per-attempt timeouts can be compared with it.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh
- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh
- .agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md

## Acceptance

- A worker with fresh DB part activity past 1500 s keeps running and gets one `worker_cap_extended` event, then is killed at the active cap if it is still output-silent.
- A worker with no fresh DB activity past 1500 s is killed exactly as today, with the same reason classification (GH#35291 behaviour unchanged).
- `WORKER_STALL_HARD_KILL_SECONDS=0` still disables the hard-kill branch.
- `test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh` passes, with cases added for an extended cap and a kill at the active cap. ShellCheck clean.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh`. After deploy, compare the `rg 'worker_killed.*hard_kill_cap_active' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-dispatch.log` rate and the `watchdog_stall_killed` slot-hours in `worker-activity-helper.sh summary` over 24 h against the figures above.

title: fix(metrics): route GH013 ruleset push rejections to the metrics PR fallback
body:
## What

`repo-metrics-git-push-helper.sh` falls back to its deterministic metrics PR only when a direct push to the default branch is rejected with `GH006: Protected branch update failed`. Repositories protected by a **ruleset** reject the same push with `GH013: Repository rule violations` ("Changes must be made through a pull request", required status checks expected). The helper treats GH013 as a transient failure, retries the direct push, and the scheduled `Repository Metrics` workflow then fails without ever opening the PR.

Route a GH013 ruleset rejection that requires a pull request into the existing PR mode, exactly as GH006 is handled today.

## Why

Observed on a managed repo's scheduled metrics run (2026-11-23): push rejected with `GH013: Repository rule violations`, no `SYNC_PAT`, no PR fallback, run failed. The CI-failure miner then filed a "Systemic CI failure: Repository Metrics" issue in that repo, which a worker correctly could not fix from the caller repo (the publish logic lives in the pinned reusable workflow). Every ruleset-protected repo using `loc-badge-reusable.yml` will hit this on its first scheduled refresh.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/repo-metrics-git-push-helper.sh` (direct-push branch, currently around the `grep -q 'GH006.*Protected branch update failed'` check near line 208), also match the GH013 ruleset rejection that requires a pull request (for example `GH013.*Repository rule violations`, plus the "must be made through a pull request" line). Keep every other push failure on the existing retry path; do not widen to arbitrary GH013 rule types that a PR would not satisfy (e.g. signed-commit or file-path rules) unless the push log also states that a pull request is required.
2. Update the PR body text (around line 71, "rejected direct publication with GH006") to name both GH006 and GH013.
3. Keep branch protection, ruleset enforcement, review and required checks untouched; no bypass, no `fail_on_push_error: false`.
4. Note: PR creation itself still needs the repo's "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" setting or a scoped `SYNC_PAT`. That is a per-repo maintainer setting and is out of scope here; the helper's existing `Cannot create metrics PR` error already reports it.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/repo-metrics-git-push-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-metrics-git-push-helper.sh` (extend the existing GH006 routing case with a GH013 ruleset fixture; reference pattern is the GH006 case in the same file)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A push log containing a GH013 "Repository rule violations" rejection that requires a pull request switches the helper into PR mode.
- [ ] GH006 behaviour unchanged; other push failures still retry without opening a PR.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean on the edited script.
- [ ] Existing metrics helper tests (if any) pass.

## Verification

title: t19337: perf(pulse): give split-lock refill passes a fresh clock so pass 2 dispatches instead of idling
body:
## Task


With `PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT=1`, a refill-only run (`pulse-wrapper.sh --refill-only`) holds only the dispatch lock and keeps the normal cycle clamp, measured from process start (`_pulse_cycle_remaining_seconds`: start + min(stale, `PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S`) − now − reserve, about 1710 s). On a busy pool, pass 1 of `pulse_event_refill_drain` uses nearly all of it. Pass 2 then always stops before enumeration on the spent clock, and the trigger stays retained until a later worker exit starts a new wake. Start each later pass of a split-lock refill-only run on a fresh clamp, so dispatch continues instead of idling.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

With `PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT=1`, a refill-only run (`pulse-wrapper.sh --refill-only`) holds only the dispatch lock and keeps the normal cycle clamp, measured from process start (`_pulse_cycle_remaining_seconds`: start + min(stale, `PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S`) − now − reserve, about 1710 s). On a busy pool, pass 1 of `pulse_event_refill_drain` uses nearly all of it. Pass 2 then always stops before enumeration on the spent clock, and the trigger stays retained until a later worker exit starts a new wake. Start each later pass of a split-lock refill-only run on a fresh clamp, so dispatch continues instead of idling.

## Why (measured 2026-11-24 08:40–12:27Z, one macOS runner, 20 slots, flag on, providers healthy)

- Dispatch ran as a sequence of single processes. Each launched 6–17 workers over 10–23 min, then a dead gap of 6–17 min followed before the next process's first ceremony (`dispatch-stages.tsv` per-pid first/last `dedup.ceremony_total`). The gaps summed to about 75 of 225 min. `pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh report` reports `ceremony_concurrency.idle_share` 0.281 and mean occupancy 9.4/20, while rounds started with 109–144 candidates.
- 4 of the 8 gaps began with `[pulse-event-refill] action=drain_failed source=worker-exit pass=2 trigger=retained`. The preceding line was `Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration: cycle wall-clock budget below dispatch reserve (remaining=-68s floor=291s ...)`. Example: pass 1 ran 11:33:35–12:02:31 and launched 17 workers. Pass 2 was refused at 12:02:49. The next wake came at 12:06:37 (3.8 min with no dispatcher), and its first ceremony started at 12:09:16.
- Since 05:02Z: 17 worker-exit drains started, 5 ended `drain_failed`, all with negative remaining budget.
- Safety is unchanged: the dispatch lock heartbeat is refreshed throughout each round (`_dispatch_refresh_owner_lease` → `pulse_dispatch_lock_heartbeat`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`), so stale reclaim (`PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S`) still applies only to a hung holder. `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_MAX_PASSES` (default 2) still bounds the process.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`: add `_pulse_event_refill_prepare_next_pass <source>` and call it in `pulse_event_refill_drain` before every pass after the first, before the trigger is moved to processing.
  - It acts only for a refill-only run (`PULSE_REFILL_ONLY=1`) under the split lock that holds the dispatch lock and not the instance lock: the same ownership test as `_pulse_event_refill_hand_off_census`. A cycle's own clock is never touched; otherwise it returns 0 and changes nothing.
  - If this process's bundle is no longer the active one (`_pulse_event_refill_wrapper_is_active "${_PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_SCRIPT_DIR}/pulse-wrapper.sh"` fails) or a runtime transition is active (`_pulse_event_refill_runtime_transition_active`), log `action=pass_deferred reason=inactive_bundle|runtime_transition trigger=retained` and stop, so an old bundle is not kept dispatching. The trigger is left for the active bundle's next wake.
  - Otherwise set `PULSE_START_EPOCH` to now, log `action=pass_clock_refreshed`, and continue.
- Reference pattern: `_pulse_event_refill_apply_budget` (same file), which resets the refill clock for the instance-lock mode.
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` or the nearest refill reference: one sentence describing the new log actions, if such a section exists.
- Touch `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh` only if an existing case covers drain passes and needs one more; add no new harness.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh
- .agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md

## Acceptance

- Split-lock refill-only run, pass 1 spends its clock, trigger re-recorded: pass 2 logs `action=pass_clock_refreshed` and runs `apply_dispatch_max` instead of `drain_failed`.
- Negative: flag off (instance-lock refill) or a cycle-owned drain (instance lock held): `PULSE_START_EPOCH` is unchanged and behaviour is identical to today.
- Negative: inactive bundle or active runtime transition: pass 2 does not start, `action=pass_deferred ... trigger=retained` is logged, and the trigger file remains.
- ShellCheck clean; existing `test-pulse-event-refill*.sh` and `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` pass.
- Runtime: after deployment, `rg 'action=drain_failed source=worker-exit pass=2'` stops appearing with negative remaining budget, and `pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh report --since <deploy>` shows `ceremony_concurrency.idle_share` below 0.281 over a comparable window.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
```

title: t19338: perf(pulse): keep the refill waker running while coalesced exits re-record the trigger
body:
## Task


`pulse_event_refill_signal` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`) holds the refill wake lock for at most `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_WAKE_PASSES` (default 2) wrapper runs. Worker exits during the last run log `action=wake_coalesced` and rely on that run, which can finish with `action=pass_limit trigger=retained`. The waker then releases the lock with a fresh trigger and no dispatcher. Nothing dispatches until another worker exit starts a new waker. Let the waker continue while each run left a newly recorded trigger.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`pulse_event_refill_signal` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`) holds the refill wake lock for at most `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_WAKE_PASSES` (default 2) wrapper runs. Worker exits during the last run log `action=wake_coalesced` and rely on that run, which can finish with `action=pass_limit trigger=retained`. The waker then releases the lock with a fresh trigger and no dispatcher. Nothing dispatches until another worker exit starts a new waker. Let the waker continue while each run left a newly recorded trigger.

## Why (measured 2026-11-24, one macOS runner, 20 slots, `PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT=1`)

- Retained triggers after the waker's last pass waited 0.5–6 min for the next exit: 09:19→09:23, 10:17→10:18, 11:16→11:17, 12:02→12:06 and 12:47:55→12:53:49. In the last case pid 35441's pass 2 ran 12:41:33–12:47:55, and the exits at 12:44:20 and 12:46:53 were `wake_coalesced` into it. A trigger retained after wake pass 1 instead starts wake pass 2 within 1–2 s.
- t19337 (GH#40162) lets pass 2 of a split-lock refill run dispatch instead of failing on a spent clock. Longer pass 2 runs collect more coalesced exits, so this stranding becomes the main reason a trigger is left without a dispatcher.
- Each new refill process also pays about 2–4.5 min of startup and enumeration before its first ceremony completes (pid 47712: wake 12:53:49, first candidate dedup 12:56:21, first ceremony 12:58:45). Continuing the existing waker does not avoid the next process's startup, but removes the wait for an unrelated exit.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`, `pulse_event_refill_signal`:
  - Before each wrapper run, record the trigger identity: its single line `issue=… worker_pid=… ts=…`. `pulse_event_refill_write_trigger` replaces the file atomically, so a new exit always changes it.
  - After `max_wake_passes` runs, continue only when the trigger exists and its identity differs from the one recorded before the last run. That means an exit was recorded during that run. A stale retained trigger (blocked gate, lock busy) keeps today's stop.
  - Bound continuations with `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_WAKE_MAX_CONTINUATIONS` (default 24; 0 restores today's behaviour). Re-resolve the wrapper with `_pulse_event_refill_resolve_wake_wrapper` before each continuation, so an activation rebases to the active bundle and a runtime transition stops with the trigger retained. Log `action=wake_continued pass=N reason=fresh_trigger`.
- The wake lock is reclaimed only when its holder dies (`_pulse_event_refill_acquire_wake_lock`), so a longer-lived waker is safe. Dispatch rounds stay serialised by the dispatch/instance lock.
- Reference pattern: the existing wake-pass loop in the same function, and `_pulse_event_refill_resolve_wake_wrapper` for rebasing.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh

## Acceptance

- A fake wrapper that writes a new trigger on its first N runs and consumes it on the last: the waker runs N+1 times with `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_WAKE_PASSES=1`, logs `wake_continued`, and leaves no trigger.
- A fake wrapper that leaves the trigger untouched: the waker stops after `max_wake_passes` runs with the trigger retained, as today.
- `PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_WAKE_MAX_CONTINUATIONS=0`: identical to today.
- ShellCheck clean; `test-pulse-event-refill.sh` and `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` pass.
- Runtime: after deployment, `action=pass_limit trigger=retained` is followed by `wake_continued` or `wake_started` within seconds, not minutes, in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
```

title: t19339: perf(pulse): let refill-only runs adopt the handed-off census instead of rescanning
body:
## Task


A refill-only Pulse run (`pulse-wrapper.sh --refill-only`) never adopts the census that the previous dispatch process handed on, so it rescans every repository (99–127 s) before its first candidate. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, `_dispatch_ranked_candidates_json` calls `_dispatch_adopt_candidate_handoff` only when `_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE == 1`, which only a cycle's first wave sets. Let a refill-only run adopt a fresh handoff census on its first enumeration as well.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

A refill-only Pulse run (`pulse-wrapper.sh --refill-only`) never adopts the census that the previous dispatch process handed on, so it rescans every repository (99–127 s) before its first candidate. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, `_dispatch_ranked_candidates_json` calls `_dispatch_adopt_candidate_handoff` only when `_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE == 1`, which only a cycle's first wave sets. Let a refill-only run adopt a fresh handoff census on its first enumeration as well.

## Why (measured 2026-11-24, one macOS runner, 20 slots)

- Refill process 35441 handed its census on at 12:47:55 (`Dispatch candidate census handed to next dispatch process: bundle=next-process mode=normalize transfer=move reuse_window=1200s`). The next refill process, 47712, started at 12:53:49, logged no `handoff adopted`/`discarded` line, and ran a full census: drain_started 12:54:06, first candidate dedup 12:56:21. Recent full censuses: `candidate enumeration timing census=full outcome=ok elapsed=99s/126s/127s`. A snapshot hit in the same process: `elapsed=1s sample=snapshot_hit`.
- Refill-only runs are now the main dispatchers between cycles (`PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT=1`), so each new process idles a freed slot for about 2 min. Today the census waits for the next cycle's first wave or expires.
- Safety is unchanged. Adopted candidates still pass the registry/schedule recheck and every live dispatch gate (comment above `_dispatch_adopt_candidate_handoff`). Eligibility mutations still invalidate the handoff, while `_dispatch_invalidate_candidate_snapshot event_refill` deliberately keeps it (line ~304). `_dispatch_candidate_snapshot_is_fresh` bounds a handed-on census to `captured_at > now - 2*handoff_window` (≤ 40 min with the default 1200 s window), so re-handing cannot keep an old census alive.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`, `_dispatch_ranked_candidates_json` (around line 615): attempt `_dispatch_adopt_candidate_handoff` when `_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE == 1` **or** `PULSE_REFILL_ONLY == 1`. Do not change the first-wave-only filters below it (`_dispatch_filter_partial_snapshot_candidates`, `_dispatch_first_wave_remainder_short`); they stay keyed on `_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE`.
- Keep the existing logs (`census handoff adopted` / `discarded`) and stats counters; the refill run hands any remainder on at exit through `_pulse_event_refill_hand_off_census` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`), as today.
- Update the GH#38048 comment above the call to say refill-only runs adopt too.
- Reference pattern: the existing first-wave adoption call and its tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh

## Acceptance

- With a fresh handoff census and `PULSE_REFILL_ONLY=1`, `_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE=0`: the handoff is installed as the refill's snapshot, `build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json` is not called, and `census handoff adopted` is logged. Add one case beside the existing first-wave adoption case; no new harness.
- An expired handoff in the same setup is discarded (`reason=stale_or_invalid`) and a full census runs, as for a first wave.
- With `PULSE_REFILL_ONLY` unset and `_PULSE_FIRST_DISPATCH_WAVE=0` (a cycle's later rounds), behaviour is unchanged: no adoption attempt.
- ShellCheck clean; `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` and `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` pass.
- Runtime: after deployment, refill-only processes log `census handoff adopted` and `candidate enumeration timing ... sample=snapshot_hit` on their first pass when the previous process handed off within the window (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`).

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
```

title: t19341: perf(runner-capability): share the readable-secret cache across pulse processes to stop check_timeout deferral bursts
body:
## Task


Share the runner-capability "secret is readable" cache across Pulse processes on the same host, so a refill-only run and a concurrent cycle do not decrypt the same gopass entries at the same time. Today the cache from GH#39815 is keyed by `_PULSE_CYCLE_ID` (`.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`, `cycle_state()`: `sha256(cycle).json`), and that ID is `<utc>-$$` for each process (`.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh:190`). Every new dispatch process starts cold. In a parallel dispatch wave several processes decrypt the same names through one gpg-agent, exceed the 12 s inner / 15 s outer secret-read timeout, and defer secret-gated candidates with `reason=check_timeout`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Share the runner-capability "secret is readable" cache across Pulse processes on the same host, so a refill-only run and a concurrent cycle do not decrypt the same gopass entries at the same time. Today the cache from GH#39815 is keyed by `_PULSE_CYCLE_ID` (`.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`, `cycle_state()`: `sha256(cycle).json`), and that ID is `<utc>-$$` for each process (`.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh:190`). Every new dispatch process starts cold. In a parallel dispatch wave several processes decrypt the same names through one gpg-agent, exceed the 12 s inner / 15 s outer secret-read timeout, and defer secret-gated candidates with `reason=check_timeout`.

## Why (measured on one macOS runner, `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, 2026-11-24)

- 933 secret-gated checks (`runner_capability_check source=fresh requirements=5`). Only 481 reused all five names (`runner_capability_secret_cache reused=5 checked=0`); the rest decrypted again.
- 23 deferrals `runner_capability_unmet reason=check_timeout`, all on secret names: `<APP>_BETA_TEST_EMAIL` ×11, `<APP>_BETA_TEST_PASSWORD` ×8, `<QA>_ADMIN_EMAIL` ×3, `<QA>_ADMIN_TOKEN` ×1 (one private managed repo; names are placeholders here). 15 of them came in one dispatch wave around 13:01Z. Cycle stages (`cleanup_stale_session_locks`, `sweep_closed_auto_dispatch_issues`) ran in one process and refill dispatches in another, so two caches were cold at once. Each deferral costs 28–37 s of a dispatch slot (`Stage failed: dispatch_candidate_<N> exited with 1 (28s)`) and puts the issue back a round (four distinct issues in that burst).
- With no contention the same check takes about 1.2 s (`/usr/bin/time -p aidevops secret check <NAME>` → `real 1.22`), so the timeouts come from concurrent load. The store was not locked.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`, `_runner_capability_python_cycle` / `_runner_capability_python_secrets`:
  - Add a host-scoped readable map file in the same `runner-capability` directory, e.g. `readable.json`. Apply the same safety checks as the cycle file (0600, `O_NOFOLLOW`, owner uid, regular file) and the same `fcntl.flock`.
  - Content: names and epoch timestamps only, never values. TTL: the existing `readable_ttl()` (`AIDEVOPS_RUNNER_CAPABILITY_READABLE_TTL_SECONDS`, default 300, max 1800).
  - In `check_secrets`, treat a name as readable when the cycle state **or** the host map has a fresh entry. Record each successful check in both.
  - Hold the host lock while decrypting a name not yet cached, so at most one process decrypts a given name at a time and waiters reuse its result. Bound the wait for that lock to the per-check secret timeout. When the wait expires, run the check directly as today (non-blocking `LOCK_NB` retry loop or similar); never wait without a bound.
  - Leave the **unreadable / locked-store** state per cycle exactly as now (`check_cached_unreadable`, `unreadable()`). The test "cycle cache skips remaining checks, permits ungated candidates and resets next cycle" (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh` ~line 502) must still pass unchanged: a new cycle re-checks a locked store.
  - A failed check (`secret_missing`, `secret_unreadable`, `check_timeout`, `check_failed`) removes that name from the host map, so a revoked or broken entry stops being reused at once.
- Keep the `runner_capability_secret_cache reused=N checked=M` stderr line. If useful, add a `source=host` count so the effect can be measured.
- Reference pattern: the GH#39815 per-cycle readable cache in the same function, and its tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh

## Acceptance

- Two calls with different `_PULSE_CYCLE_ID` values within the TTL decrypt each readable name once; the second call's stub `aidevops secret check` is not invoked. Extend the existing cycle-cache test fixture; no new harness.
- An expired host entry is re-checked. A failing re-check removes the name from the host map.
- The locked-store test (unreadable state resets next cycle) and the timeout-does-not-cache test pass unchanged.
- The host map contains only `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*` names and numeric timestamps (assert no value bytes, as the existing `PRIVATE_` assertions do).
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh` clean; `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh` passes.
- Runtime: after deployment, `rg -c 'runner_capability_unmet reason=check_timeout' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` grows much more slowly than the baseline of 23 per day. `runner_capability_secret_cache reused=` lines rise as a share of `source=fresh requirements=5` checks.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh
```

Related: GH#39815 (per-cycle readable cache), GH#38172, GH#34427.
