title: t19342: fix(routines): keep routine run output out of pulse.log (1.18 MB per run shrinks the hot diagnostic window)
body:
## Task


Stop appending each scheduled routine run's full headless output (the opencode JSON event stream, including tool results) to `pulse.log`. Keep that output in a bounded per-routine log file. Write one summary line to `pulse.log` with the outcome and the file path.

Today `_routine_run_detached_agent` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh` (around line 640) captures the run into a temp `output_file`, parses `ROUTINE_OUTCOME`, then runs `cat "$output_file" >>"$LOGFILE"`. Before GH#39730 the stdout was redirected to `$LOGFILE` directly, so the dump is long-standing.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop appending each scheduled routine run's full headless output (the opencode JSON event stream, including tool results) to `pulse.log`. Keep that output in a bounded per-routine log file. Write one summary line to `pulse.log` with the outcome and the file path.

Today `_routine_run_detached_agent` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh` (around line 640) captures the run into a temp `output_file`, parses `ROUTINE_OUTCOME`, then runs `cat "$output_file" >>"$LOGFILE"`. Before GH#39730 the stdout was redirected to `$LOGFILE` directly, so the dump is long-standing.

## Why (measured 2026-11-24 on one macOS runner)

- One routine run (`routine-r-<private>-…`, 13:00Z) wrote 744 JSON event lines (`{"type":"step_start"|"tool_use"|"text"|"step_finish",…}`), 1,180,450 bytes. That is 20% of the 5,772,269-byte hot `pulse.log`.
- `rotate_pulse_log` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh`) rotates at `PULSE_LOG_HOT_MAX_BYTES`, so every routine dump shortens the hot diagnostic window that dispatch and throughput investigations read; today's hot log only starts at 05:02Z. It also slows every bounded `rg` over `pulse.log`.
- The stream carries raw tool output (webfetch bodies, command output) from private repositories into the shared diagnostic log. That log is routinely quoted when filing issues, which leaves the privacy guard as the only safeguard.
- Issue workers already keep their stream in a per-session `output_file` (see `output_file` in `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`). Routines should follow the same pattern.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`, `_routine_run_detached_agent`:

title: t19343: fix(trigger-revisit): recognise GH#N, issue N, PR N and phase N refs so blocked holds wake when their named issue resolves
body:
## Task


Teach the terminal-blocker trigger-revisit parser (`_tbtr_trigger_refs` in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh`) the same-repository reference forms workers actually write in `Trigger awaited:` lines: `GH#N`, `issue N`, `PR N` / `pull request N` and `phase N`. Then re-parse existing holds that were stored with an empty `trigger_refs` list. Today only a bare `#N` not preceded by a letter, digit or `/` is recognised, so these holds never get the t19245 early wake when the named issue closes or PR merges. They sit `status:blocked` until the next scheduled revisit, which starts at one day and doubles up to seven (`AIDEVOPS_TRIGGER_REVISIT_INTERVAL_S` default 86400, `_TBTR_MAX_INTERVAL=604800`).

<details>

## Task Brief

## What

Today only a bare `#N` not preceded by a letter, digit or `/` is recognised, so these holds never get the t19245 early wake when the named issue closes or PR merges. ## Why (measured 2026-11-24 on one runner, `~/.aidevops/logs/terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit/`)

- 104 revisit records. 18 waiting holds (`scheduled`/`still_pending`) have `trigger_refs: []`. In 5 of them the trigger names a same-repository issue or PR that the regex misses (private managed repo, so the text is abbreviated):
  - `Issue <N> (people phase) closed, or …` (bare `Issue N`)
  - `GH#<N> (…) merges to develop` (`GH#N`: the `H` before `#` fails `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9/])#`)
  - `merge of the binder fix for issue <N> (worker PR <M>) into develop`
  - `Media phase <N> reconciles …, and closes again`
  - `Results phase <N> completes and records …`
- Example: a hold created 12:12:53Z with an empty refs list is next due at +24 h (`next_at=1795608773`), whenever its named issue closes. That repository has 303 open `status:blocked` issues; the sampled holds are mostly phase chains that name a sibling issue number.
- The remaining 13 empty-ref holds name dated external events (ceremonies, publications); the scheduled revisit already covers those. Out of scope.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh`, `_tbtr_trigger_refs` (line ~143):
  - Keep the existing `#N` rule, including the exclusion of `owner/repo#N` cross-repo refs.
  - Also accept `GH#N` (case-insensitive `GH`, not preceded by a letter, digit or `/`).
  - Also accept keyword forms, case-insensitive: `issue`, `PR`, `pull request`, `phase`, followed by whitespace, an optional `#`, then the number. In the keyword forms only, require at least 3 digits, so `phase 2` or `PR 1` style ordinals are not read as refs. Issue numbers in managed repos are far larger.
  - Keep `unique` and the `.[:3]` cap.
  - A false ref costs little: an open or unreadable ref blocks the early wake (`_tbtr_refs_resolved` returns false), which is today's behaviour, and the AI decision still judges every wake.
- Backfill: add a parser version to the record, e.g. `refs_parser: 2`, written by `_tbtr_record_scheduled` (line ~309) together with `trigger_refs`. In `_tbtr_ref_wake_due` (line ~172), treat a waiting record with an empty `trigger_refs` and no `refs_parser >= 2` like a record without `trigger_refs`: return 0 once, so the next pass does the full read and re-parses the trigger. Keep the existing behaviour for records with refs.
- Reference pattern: the t19245 ref-wake design and `_trigger_revisit_ref_wake_cases` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (~line 699).

- .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh

  - `Media phase 32312 reconciles` → `32312`

title: runner-capability: detect host IPC failure (getpwuid, trustd TLS, Chromium bootstrap) and defer dispatch without claiming
body:
## Problem

On a macOS runner, a host-level IPC fault lasted about 90 minutes (2026-11-24, roughly 14:50 to 16:20 UTC). During it the pulse kept dispatching headless workers that could not complete their tasks. Every worker failed in the same way after it had claimed its issue:

- Playwright Chromium launch: `bootstrap_check_in org.chromium.Chromium.MachPortRendezvousServer.<pid>: Permission denied (1100)`.
- `gh auth status`: `x509: OSStatus -26276` (trustd unreachable; Go TLS verification uses the system trust service).
- `git ls-remote origin`: the credential helper failed with `failed to get: -50`, then `could not read Username`.
- `id -un` printed the numeric uid; `log show` reported `getpwuid_r did not find a match for uid 501` and `Connection to logd failed`; `pgrep` reported `sysmond service not found`.

It was not a seatbelt sandbox (`sandbox_check` returned 0 for every ancestor process) and it was not sustained load. The daemons were running. A Mac restart cleared it.

Effects observed:

- Five workers failed within four minutes with the Chromium error, each after claiming its issue (`status:in-progress` plus assignee). The claims stayed after the host recovered, so those issues waited for stale-claim expiry before redispatch.
- One worker could not push a finished commit (credential helper failure), leaving work only on local disk until an interactive session found and pushed it.
- An interactive guarded write waited about 519 s for a shared sign-in lock, then failed at Chromium launch. Nothing was written, but the lock slot was spent.

`runner-capability-helper.sh` already returns `runner_health` verdicts that defer candidates without claiming (Node requirement at `_runner_capability_project_node_verdict`, locked gpg store in `_runner_capability_python_secrets`, see #33638). No check covers host IPC health, so `runner_capability_check source=fresh requirements=0` passes on a host where no worker can launch a browser or reach GitHub with TLS.

## Proposed fix

Add a cheap, cached host-IPC probe to the runner capability path. When it fails, all candidates on that runner defer without claiming, and the runner emits one `runner_health:` line per recheck interval.

Probe candidates (each bounded to a few seconds; any failure means unhealthy):

1. `id -un` returns a non-numeric name (detects `getpwuid` / opendirectoryd loss).
2. `gh auth status --hostname github.com` or an equivalent TLS handshake through the system trust store completes without `OSStatus` errors (detects trustd loss). `curl` is not a valid probe: it uses its own CA store and passed during the fault.
3. Optional, only when the repository declares a browser requirement or the runner opts in: a bare headless Playwright Chromium launch-and-close (detects the Mach bootstrap failure). Cache the result for the recheck interval so it does not run per candidate.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`: add `_runner_capability_host_ipc_verdict` next to `_runner_capability_project_node_verdict`, cached per pulse cycle like the readable-secret cache (#40166), and call it from `runner_capability_check` before per-issue requirements.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`: if the gate distinguishes runner-wide from per-issue deferrals, classify the new verdict as runner-wide, so it pauses the runner instead of cooling down individual issues (compare #39779).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh`: add cases with stubbed `id` and `gh` that return the failure shapes above, and a healthy case.

## Reference pattern

title: t19345: perf(process-snapshot): use TZ=UTC0 for macOS full-table ps lstart reads
body:
## Task


On macOS, `ps -axo ...,lstart=` loads a time-zone file for every row when `TZ`
is unset or set to a zone name such as `UTC`. Two hot readers poll the full
process table this way:

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh` `_sandbox_snapshot_descendants_ps`
(every 0.5 s per running worker) and its revalidation partner
`_sandbox_get_proc_starttime`.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-snapshot.mjs`
`processSnapshot()` (every 250 ms per bounded operation, 1 s timeout).

`TZ=UTC0` is a POSIX zone string, so no zone file is loaded.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

On macOS, `ps -axo ...,lstart=` loads a time-zone file for every row when `TZ`
is unset or set to a zone name such as `UTC`. Two hot readers poll the full
process table this way:

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh` `_sandbox_snapshot_descendants_ps`
  (every 0.5 s per running worker) and its revalidation partner
  `_sandbox_get_proc_starttime`.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-snapshot.mjs`
  `processSnapshot()` (every 250 ms per bounded operation, 1 s timeout).

`TZ=UTC0` is a POSIX zone string, so no zone file is loaded.

## Why (measured 2026-11-24 on one macOS host, ~1,000-1,300 processes)

| Read | TZ unset | TZ=UTC | TZ=UTC0 | no lstart |
|------|----------|--------|---------|-----------|
| wall ms | 586 | 385 | 38 | 33 |
| CPU ms | 195 | 110 | 22 | 22 |

- At load average ~170 the unset read averaged 985 ms, right at the 1 s
  `processSnapshot()` timeout. A timed-out read returns `null` and marks
  attribution incomplete.
- `_sandbox_snapshot_descendants_ps`: 200 ms -> 35 ms per call. The recorded
  token still equals `_sandbox_get_proc_starttime`.
- `processSnapshot()`: 190 ms -> 23 ms per call, no null snapshots.
- `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=UTC0` output were byte-identical on 1,049 rows.
- At 14 concurrent workers (28 snapshot polls/s), ps CPU drops from ~5.5
  cores to ~0.6 cores.

## How

- Prefix both sandbox lstart reads with `TZ=UTC0 LC_ALL=C`. They must stay
  identical because cleanup and the watchdog revalidate snapshot tokens.
- Set `TZ: "UTC0"` in the `processSnapshot()` spawn env. Its identities are
  compared only within one in-memory tracker.
- Linux paths read `/proc` and are unchanged.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-snapshot.mjs

## Acceptance

- Both full-table macOS lstart reads run with `TZ=UTC0`. The single-PID
  sandbox revalidation uses the same zone and locale.
- Snapshot tokens still match `_sandbox_get_proc_starttime`.
- Existing sandbox and bounded-operation tests pass.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs
```

## Not in scope

Single-PID `lstart` callers load one zone file per call, which is cheap.
`process_termination_identity.py` reads the full table with `TZ=UTC` only on
kill/listener policy checks, which are infrequent. `TZ=UTC0` would give
identical output if it ever becomes a hot path.

Related: parent productivity work in GH#40108.

</details>

title: t19346: fix(pulse): break early in stats quarantine scan and prune the backlog
body:
<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


Target repository: marcusquinn/aidevops

## Problem

`_pulse_stats_recover_locked` quarantines a corrupt `pulse-stats.json` before
reinitialising it. GH#37776 (commit `5231638d02`, 2026-11-11) correctly capped new
quarantine copies at 5, but two gaps remain on installs that accumulated a
pre-cap backlog:

1. **No early break in the duplicate scan.** `.agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh:121-128`
   globs every `pulse-stats.json.corrupt.*` file into an array and runs `cmp -s`
   against each one on every recovery attempt, even after `count` has passed the
   cap of 5. The cap is only consulted afterwards at line 129. With a large
   backlog this spawns one `cmp` subprocess per quarantine file per recovery.
2. **No pruning path.** `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh` has no
   handling for these files: `rg -n 'corrupt|quarantine|pulse-stats'` against it
   returns no matches. Nothing in the storage-hygiene routine reclaims them, so
   the backlog and its per-recovery scan cost persist indefinitely.

## Observed evidence

On one Linux install (aidevops v3.39.277):

- `fd -H -t f -g 'pulse-stats.json.corrupt.*' ~/.aidevops/logs | wc -l` -> `16408`
- `~/.aidevops/logs` shrank from 966M to 901M after deleting them, i.e. ~65 MB
  held by quarantine copies alone.
- File mtimes spanned 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-27; sizes ranged from 16 B to 787 KB.
  No new quarantine file has appeared since 2026-10-27, so the underlying
  corruption is not currently reproducing and is NOT part of this task.
- Two samples were preserved for reference before deletion (16 B and 787 KB).

The 16408-file scan is therefore a real cost on any install that accumulated a
backlog before the cap landed: every corruption recovery would fork 16408 `cmp`
processes while holding the stats lock.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh`

## Required changes

`.agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh`: add an early `break` in the quarantine
enumeration loop at lines 121-128 once the cap and duplicate checks can no
longer change the outcome. Keep the existing duplicate detection semantics for
backlogs under the cap: the loop must still be able to observe a duplicate, so
break only when `count` has reached the cap AND a duplicate has already been
found, or restructure so the cap short-circuits without changing behaviour for
small backlogs. Do not raise or remove the cap.

`.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh`: prune `pulse-stats.json.corrupt.*`
beyond the retained cap (keep the newest few as evidence), consistent with how
this helper already treats other reclaimable log artifacts.

## Reference pattern

Follow the existing guarded-glob and `nullglob` restore style already used in
`_pulse_stats_recover_locked` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh:119-122`),
and the existing size/age-based reclamation entries in
`.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh` for the pruning addition.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh .agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh`
  must report zero violations.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` for the changed files.
- Create a scratch directory with, say, 50 `pulse-stats.json.corrupt.*` files
  plus a deliberately invalid `pulse-stats.json`, trigger one recovery, and
  confirm the recovery still reinitialises the stats file, still refuses to add
  a sixth quarantine copy, and no longer scans every backlog file.
- Confirm the storage-cleanup addition reports the reclaimed count and retains
  the newest evidence copies.

## Out of scope

The root cause of the original `pulse-stats.json` corruption (last observed
2026-10-27) is not part of this task; no active reproduction is available.

</details>

title: t19347: fix(pulse): report the configured interval and live worker cap in pulse start
body:
<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


Target repository: marcusquinn/aidevops

## Problem

The `aidevops pulse start` / pulse session summary prints two values that do not
reflect configuration, which misleads operators who are tuning capacity:

1. **Hardcoded interval.** `.agents/scripts/pulse-session-helper.sh:324` prints
   `"  Pulse interval: every 2 minutes (via ${scheduler_name})"` as a literal
   string. It never reads `orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds`, whose default
   has been 180 s since t2744. Any operator-configured interval is misreported.
2. **Stale worker cap.** The same summary reads `MAX_WORKERS_FILE`
   (`.agents/scripts/pulse-session-helper.sh:42`, used at lines 314 and 668),
   i.e. `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-max-workers`. That cache is only refreshed by a
   pulse capacity pass, so after a config change — or while pulse is paused — it
   reports the previous ceiling.

## Observed evidence

On one Linux install (aidevops v3.39.277), after setting
`orchestration.max_workers_cap: 12` in `~/.config/aidevops/config.jsonc`:

- `aidevops pulse start` printed `Max workers: 18` and
  `Pulse interval: every 2 minutes`.
- Authoritative state at the same moment: `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-health.json`
  -> `{"workers_max": 12, "workers_active": 0}`, and `pulse.log` wrote
  `pulse-health.json written: workers=0/12`.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-max-workers` contained `18` with mtime
  `2026-11-23 18:56`, i.e. ~22 hours stale.
- `systemctl --user show aidevops-supervisor-pulse.timer --property=TimersMonotonic`
  -> `OnUnitActiveUSec=3min`, `OnBootUSec=3min`; `settings.json` had
  `orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds: 180`. The real interval was 3 minutes,
  not the 2 printed.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-session-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh`

## Required changes

`.agents/scripts/pulse-session-helper.sh`: derive the printed interval from the
configured value instead of the literal `every 2 minutes`, and prefer a live
worker cap over the cache for both summary sites (lines 314 and 668). Keep the
existing `?` fallback when no source is readable.

`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh` is in scope only if a shared
interval reader has to be reused or extracted from
`_read_pulse_interval_seconds` (line 531), which already resolves
`.orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds // .supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds`
from the settings file with a 180 default and a [30, 3600] clamp. Do not
duplicate that clamp logic — reuse or extract it.

## Reference pattern

- Interval resolution: `_read_pulse_interval_seconds` in
  `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh:531-537`.
- Live worker cap: `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-health.json` `.workers_max`, written
  by the pulse wrapper on every cycle (the `pulse-health.json written:
  workers=N/M` log line). Fall back to the existing `pulse-max-workers` cache,
  then `?`.
- Pluralisation must handle a single minute and non-integer minute values
  (e.g. 90 s) without printing a misleading rounded figure.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-session-helper.sh` — zero violations.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` for the changed file.
- With `orchestration.pulse_interval_seconds: 180` and
  `orchestration.max_workers_cap: 12`, confirm the summary prints a 3-minute

title: pulse: self-runner in-progress claims orphaned when worker exit-path CLAIM_RELEASED write fails are never swept
body:
## Observed

A host IPC outage at about 15:15 UTC killed every headless worker on one runner. Chromium failed with `bootstrap_check_in ... Permission denied (1100)`, and `worker-bus-relay` writes were deferred by `rest-gate`. The workers exited (`[lifecycle] worker_exited ... wait_status=unknown kill_reason=observed`), but none of them posted a `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment. Their issues stayed `status:in-progress` and assigned to the runner's own login with an expired `DISPATCH_LEASE` (`expires_at` about one hour earlier).

Nothing reclaimed them for more than 3 hours. `pulse.log` has no `Stale assignment reset` entry, and the issues never reappeared as dispatch candidates. The pulse kept dispatching other work, so launch slots were not the cause.

Running the dispatcher's own guarded path by hand released them at once:

```text
dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned <N> <managed-repo> <self-login>
STALE_RECOVERED: issue #<N> ... unassigned <self-login> (dispatch claim 11730s old, last activity 11719s old (threshold=600s, interactive=false))
```

`is-assigned-read-only` on the same issue just before reported `ASSIGNED ... to <self-login>` and offered no stale hint.

## Likely cause

`_is_stale_assignment` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`) runs only through `is-assigned` during candidate evaluation. Candidate listing excludes `status:in-progress`, so a self-runner claim whose worker died without its exit-path release is never evaluated. The normal release relies on the worker's exit trap posting `CLAIM_RELEASED`. When that GitHub write fails (rest-gate deferral, network or host outage), nothing retries it, and no sweep covers same-device in-progress issues whose registered worker PID is gone.

## Suggested fix

- Add a bounded per-cycle sweep in the pulse. For each open `status:in-progress` issue assigned to the runner login whose latest `DISPATCH_CLAIM`/`DISPATCH_LEASE` carries this runner's `device=`, check whether the registered worker PID is dead or the lease has expired. If so, call the existing `_is_stale_assignment` path, keeping its open-PR, branch-activity and interactive-fence guards.
- Alternatively, or as well, queue a failed exit-path `CLAIM_RELEASED` write durably and replay it on the next cycle.

## Verification

- Kill a dispatched worker with the GitHub write path blocked, then restore it. The issue should return to `status:available` within one pulse cycle after the lease expires, with a `STALE_RECOVERED` or replayed `CLAIM_RELEASED` record.
- A live worker, an issue with an open PR, and an interactive claim must remain untouched (the existing guards).
- Relevant tests: `tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale*.sh` and the `_recover_stale_assignment` cases.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile-orphaned-self-claim.sh`

title: t19348: fix(bounded-operation): supervisor exits by natural drain to avoid Node 26 process.exit deadlock
body:
## Task


`bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs` ends with `process.exit(await runSupervisor())`.
On Node 26 that call can deadlock (upstream nodejs/node#67596, open). The main
thread joins the V8 platform workers in `WorkerThreadsTaskRunner::Shutdown()`.
One of those workers is a concurrent compile job that is parked, waiting for a
GC that only the main thread can run. The process then:

- sits at 0% CPU forever;
- ignores SIGTERM, because its JS handler needs the blocked main loop;
- keeps its operation (or a synchronous caller) open until an outer budget.

Fix: set `process.exitCode`, release the IPC `message`/`disconnect` listeners
(they keep the channel referenced) and let the event loop drain. A natural exit
disposes the isolate before the platform workers are joined. An unref'd 2 s
`process.exit` fallback covers an unexpected lingering handle only.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs` ends with `process.exit(await runSupervisor())`.
On Node 26 that call can deadlock (upstream nodejs/node#67596, open). The main
thread joins the V8 platform workers in `WorkerThreadsTaskRunner::Shutdown()`.
One of those workers is a concurrent compile job that is parked, waiting for a
GC that only the main thread can run. The process then:

- sits at 0% CPU forever;
- ignores SIGTERM, because its JS handler needs the blocked main loop;
- keeps its operation (or a synchronous caller) open until an outer budget.

Fix: set `process.exitCode`, release the IPC `message`/`disconnect` listeners
(they keep the channel referenced) and let the event loop drain. A natural exit
disposes the isolate before the platform workers are joined. An unref'd 2 s
`process.exit` fallback covers an unexpected lingering handle only.

## Why (observed 2026-11-24 on one macOS host, Node v26.12.0)

- A `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` validator run timed out after 1500 s on
  `npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`. The stuck child was a
  fixture supervisor spawned by `tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`. `sample`
  showed the exact upstream signature: main thread in
  `Environment::Exit -> DisposePlatform -> WorkerThreadsTaskRunner::Shutdown ->
  uv_thread_join`; worker thread in Maglev `GenerateDeoptimizationData ->
  TriggerAndWaitForGCFromBackgroundThread`. That test's `execFileSync` 10 s
  timeout sends SIGTERM, which the wedged supervisor never handles.
- Upstream reproducer (`--max-old-space-size=24`, 120 runs, 12 parallel):
  `process.exit(0)` hung 2/120; natural exit (`process.exitCode`) hung 0/120.
- With `--stress-concurrent-allocation` (forces parked background
  allocations): `process.exit(0)` hung 40/40 on v26.12.0 and 20/20 on
  v24.19.0; natural exit hung 0/40 and 0/20. The hazard is in the exit path
  itself; Node 26 makes it reachable without stress flags.
- One plugin test run spawns many supervisors, so a small per-exit risk
  compounds into frequent validator timeouts for interactive full-loop and
  worker PRs alike.

## How

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs`: new
  exported `exitWhenDrained(code)` replaces the entrypoint `process.exit`.
  Signal listeners stay registered (Node signal handles do not keep the loop
  alive), so a late SIGTERM still runs the terminator instead of killing the
  process with a signal status.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`:
  `runOperation` uses `killSignal: "SIGKILL"`, so its 10 s timeout bounds any
  future exit wedge instead of blocking the suite.

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs

## Acceptance

- The supervisor's normal, admission-refused (75) and invalid-config (125)
  paths exit through a natural drain, with the same exit codes.
- Bounded-operation, git-safety-gate, dispatch-launcher, worktree-ownership
  and redaction suites pass. The admission-refused path exits in about 0.4 s,
  under the 2 s fallback.

## Verification

```bash
cd .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops
node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs \
  tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs tests/test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs \
  tests/test-bounded-worktree-ownership.mjs tests/test-registered-value-redaction.mjs
```

## Not in scope

The other `process.exit()` callers in `.agents/scripts/*.mjs` are on-demand
browser/QA tools or long-lived bridges that exit once per session. None showed
a wedge on this host. Revisit them only with evidence. The escalation-path
`process.exit(1)` in `createTerminator` runs only when signalling the
supervisor's own group fails.

Related: GH#40195 (its PR validators hit this hang); parent productivity work
in GH#40108.

</details>

title: terminal-blocker: dated reopen conditions on blocked exits are re-armed on short backoff, causing redispatch loops
body:
## Observed

In a private managed repo, one award-enrichment phase issue had two remaining ledger rows:

- a temporary source failure (an official API returned HTTP 500). The brief says to recheck after 24 h.
- a source consent hold.

Its two-session budget was also spent: two partial PRs had merged. Between 10:11Z and 17:37Z on 2026-11-24, it was dispatched six times across three runners. Each worker ended `blocked` within 2–5 minutes, and none posted a public terminal-blocker observation. Each time, another runner's re-arm path returned the issue to `status:available` 10–50 minutes later. The supervisor queue entry arrived as `intake: remote_observation`, `reason: unknown`.

The repo brief tells workers to end a temporary 5xx with `BLOCKED: source_exhausted` and the reopen condition "recheck after 24 h". The published circuit and observation evidence did not carry that reopen time, so the hold was re-armed on short backoff, which caused the loop. The supervisor stopped it manually: `status:blocked` plus an `external_trigger` record with `recheck_after`.

## Expected

When a blocked exit names a dated reopen condition (for example "recheck after 24 h" or "after <date>"), the runtime does one of two things:

- records it as `external_trigger_pending` with a machine-readable recheck time, or
- keeps the hold until that time on every runner.

Unknown-class short backoff should not apply in that case. Separately, an issue whose brief declares a two-session cap, with two merged partial PRs, should not be redispatched before the supervisor's `session_cap_split` decision.

## Files to modify

Exact paths need discovery. Likely candidates:

- the worker blocked-exit classifier (the terminal-blocker reason parsing in the headless runtime / worker exit path)
- `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (the `rearm` pass and the remote observation intake)

Reference pattern: the `external_trigger` `recheck_after` handling added in GH#40120.

## Verification

- Replay a worker exit text containing `BLOCKED: source_exhausted` plus "recheck after 24 h". Confirm the published observation records a recheck time.
- Confirm that `rearm` on another runner leaves the issue blocked until that time.
- Run existing ShellCheck and the terminal-blocker helper tests.

title: Canonical git guard blocks composer source-package clones inside linked worktrees
body:
## Problem

The PATH git shim (`agents/scripts/git` → `canonical-git-command-guard.py`) treats every standalone clone as a canonical checkout. Dependency managers that install packages from source make nested `git` calls inside fresh clones. Composer (`preferred-install: source`), for example, runs `git clone` and then `git remote set-url` inside `vendor/...` or `web/app/plugins/<pkg>`. Those calls are blocked with `canonical worktree mutation via 'git remote'`. As a result, `composer install` in a session-owned linked worktree fails halfway, which leaves the autoloader stale.

## Observed

- 2026-11-24, OpenCode 2.2.5, aidevops 3.39.189.
- `composer install` ran in a Bedrock linked runtime worktree. It cloned `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector` and then failed at `Git.php line 659` with the guard message. By then, several packages were already upgraded and the autoload dump had not run.

## Expected

Git calls whose working tree is a newly created, non-registered clone nested inside a linked worktree should be allowed: dependency trees under the worktree path. Alternatively, there should be a documented, audited way to run a dependency manager without the shim. Canonical user repositories (the primary checkout of each repository) must stay protected.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/git`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`

## Verification

`composer install` with source-preferred VCS packages succeeds inside a linked worktree, and `git remote set-url` in a canonical checkout is still blocked.

title: hostinger: document hPanel's hidden 30-minute cron kill (flock + timeout -s 9 1800) in cron docs and cron create
body:
## What

hPanel (Hostinger) runs every cron command inside a hidden wrapper that SIGKILLs it after 30 minutes:

```text
/bin/sh -c /usr/bin/flock -w 1 /tmp/cron_lock_<job-uid> timeout -s 9 1800 <command as listed in hPanel>
```

`hostinger-helper.sh cron list` shows only `<command>`, so the limit is invisible. Neither `services/hosting/hostinger.md` nor `services/hosting/hostinger-wordpress-cron.md` mentions it.

## Evidence (24 Nov 2026, a Hostinger Cloud plan account)

- `ps -o pid,ppid,etime,args` during a run of a job made with `hostinger-helper.sh cron create` showed the chain `flock -w 1 /tmp/cron_lock_<uid>` → `timeout -s 9 1800 /bin/bash <script>` → script. The lock name equals the job uid from `cron list`; the same wrapper was on every other job on the account.
- A job designed for 45-minute rounds (`rclone copy` under its own `timeout --kill-after=60 <secs>`) was killed at 30 minutes every round. Its child, a GNU `timeout` (which makes its own process group), escaped the group kill and ran on as an orphan (PPID 1) until its own deadline, still holding the script's inherited `flock` file descriptor. So the work continued, but every step after the long command (round notes, final verification, state transition) never ran. Rounds ended silently with no log line.
- Rounds capped at 25 minutes then ran to completion and logged normally.

## Proposed change

1. `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger-wordpress-cron.md` (and a one-line pointer in `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`): document the wrapper and the 30-minute SIGKILL. Long jobs must be resumable rounds that finish well under 30 minutes (25 suggested), with their own deadline, and must not rely on code after a long child command if that child can outlive the script.
2. `hostinger-helper.sh cron create` help/output: print a one-line notice of the 30-minute limit when creating a job. Optionally `cron list --verbose` could explain that the shown command is wrapped.

## Verification

- Docs: the limit and the rounds pattern appear in `hostinger-wordpress-cron.md`; markdownlint clean.
- Helper: `hostinger-helper.sh cron create --help` (or its dry-run output) shows the notice; ShellCheck clean.
- Runtime (optional, needs a Hostinger account): a test job running `sleep 2000; echo done >> file` never writes `done`, and `ps` shows the wrapper.

From the canonical cwd, `_worktree_is_allowed` (`.agents/scripts/canonical_git_ref_queries.py:15-16`) already restricts `worktree` to `list`/`add`, so the linked-worktree path is an inconsistent shortcut. ## Why it matters now GH#40211 (PR for nested Composer packages) exempts unregistered `.aidevops.json` marker repos nested below a linked worktree whose metadata lives in a registered repo's `.git/worktrees/`. The independent closeout review noted that `git worktree repair

` from a linked worktree can rewrite a genuine metadata `gitdir` back-link to point at an arbitrary ancestor `P` (with a hand-written `P/.git`), making marker-only canonical checkouts under `P` look nested. Registered repos are unaffected (checked first), and marker-only protection is already partial (file tools can delete the marker), so this is hardening, not an active exposure. ## How 1. In `classify_git_argv` (`.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py:290-320`), before returning the non-canonical allow for `subcommand == "worktree"`, apply the canonical worktree policy when the effective repository's common dir is registered/managed (`is_registered_common_dir` from `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py`): allow `list`, `add`, and the existing audited `remove` path (`_is_linked_worktree_remove_for_canonical`); block `repair`, `move`, `prune`, `lock`, `unlock` with a message naming `canonical-recovery-helper.sh repair-worktrees` (already used for canonical `worktree repair`). 2. title: t19349: fix(pulse): throughput report counts still-running workers so windows ending now are not under-reported
body:
## Task


`pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh report` under-reports worker-slot occupancy for any window that ends near "now". Occupancy is built only from spawn→exit pairs, so every worker still running at report time is left out of the samples near the end of the window. GH#40108 judges its phases on this number, so the error can steer that decision.

Fix: count each spawn without a later exit as an open interval, and report it next to the paired-only figure.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh report` under-reports worker-slot occupancy for any window that ends near "now". Occupancy is built only from spawn→exit pairs, so every worker still running at report time is left out of the samples near the end of the window. GH#40108 judges its phases on this number, so the error can steer that decision.

Fix: count each spawn without a later exit as an open interval, and report it next to the paired-only figure.

## Why (measured 2026-11-24 on one macOS runner, 20 slots)

| Window (UTC) | Report run at | Paired-only mean | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17:45–20:30 | 20:40 | **6.15** (max 12) | About 15 workers were alive at 20:40 (`ps`: 16 distinct `headless-runtime-helper.sh run --session-key issue-*`) |

title: t19350: perf(pulse): split-lock cycle entry wakes a detached refill instead of leavin...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19350` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-24
**Tags:** `feat` `priority:high`

## Outcome

perf(pulse): split-lock cycle entry wakes a detached refill instead of leaving free slots until after preflight

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

With `PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT=1`, a Pulse cycle that starts with a retained worker-exit refill trigger only logs `action=drain_completed source=cycle-entry pass=0 dispatch=deferred trigger=retained` and leaves the trigger for its own first dispatch round. That round runs after the cycle's preflight (`stale_blocked_reconcile`, `prefetch_state`, …), often 5–15 minutes later. Free slots stay empty for that time: no dispatch-lock holder is running, and the waker that left the trigger has already exited (`lock_busy` or `runtime_transition` deferral).

Fix: in split-lock mode, the cycle-entry drain wakes the existing detached refill path (`pulse_event_refill_wake_underfilled`, GH#38696) instead of only deferring. The waker coalesces on the wake lock, rebases to the active bundle, and takes only the dispatch lock. It can therefore launch while the cycle holds the instance lock through preflight. Flag off: unchanged.

## Why (measured 2026-11-24 on one macOS runner, 20 slots, split-lock canary)

| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Cycle-entry deferrals, 05:05–22:40Z (host IPC outage 14:45–16:25Z excluded) | 23 | `[pulse-event-refill] action=drain_completed source=cycle-entry … dispatch=deferred` in `pulse.log` |
| Minutes from deferral to the next ceremony start, summed | 93 min (max 14.8 min; 10 events ≥ 3.6 min) | `pulse-stage-timings.log` `dispatch_candidate_*` starts |
| Free slot-hours in those intervals | 19.9 | PR #40221 report modules (worker intervals) |
| Example, 19:28:52Z cycle (pid 38504) | 13.3 min until first ceremony; 9–14 free; stages in between: `stale_blocked_reconcile` 168 s, `prefetch_state` 402 s | stage timings |
| Free slot-time after recovery, 16:25–22:40Z | 25% no ceremony running, 48% fewer ceremonies than free slots, 27% covered | same modules |

A woken refill still needs its own census (~2–3 min) unless it adopts a handoff. The expected recovery is about 12 slot-hours per 16 h, roughly +0.75 mean occupancy against today's 9.45.

Why it was deferred: GH#32688. An in-process cycle-entry `apply_dispatch_max` consumed the whole cycle before preflight. A detached, dispatch-lock-only waker cannot do that, because it is a separate process and the cycle keeps its own budget. In split mode, cycle dispatch rounds already skip while a refill holds the dispatch lock: 61 `Dispatch stage … skipped` lines today, against 23 `event_refill_drain` and 11 cycle-round acquisitions. So this adds no new interaction.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`:
  - `pulse_event_refill_wake_underfilled`: accept an optional refill source (`$1`, default `active-pulse`; the same charset check as `pulse_event_refill_signal`), so the attribution says `cycle-entry`.
  - `pulse_event_refill_drain`, cycle-entry branch: when the trigger exists and `_pulse_event_refill_split_lock` succeeds, call `pulse_event_refill_wake_underfilled cycle-entry` and log `action=drain_completed source=cycle-entry pass=0 dispatch=woken trigger=retained`. Otherwise keep today's `dispatch=deferred` line.
  - Update the branch comment: shared-lock mode still defers (GH#32688). Split mode wakes a detached refill.
- No change to `apply_dispatch_max`, locks or budgets.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`

## Acceptance

- Split mode, trigger present at cycle entry: one detached `signal 0 <cycle pid> cycle-entry` wake starts. No in-process `apply_dispatch_max` runs.
- Flag off, or no trigger: behaviour and log lines unchanged.
- After deploy on the canary runner, `pulse.log` shows `dispatch=woken` at cycle entry, followed by `wake_started … source=cycle-entry` and `drain_started source=cycle-entry` before the cycle's `preflight_prefetch_and_scope` completes. `cycle_entry_cost`-style measurement: deferral-to-first-ceremony falls toward the census time (~2–3 min).
- `shellcheck` clean; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh` passes.

## Verification

```bash
rg -n 'source=cycle-entry' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -5
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh
```

For #40108 (Phase 1 follow-up; t19324 / PR #40121 added the split lock, GH#38696 added the underfill wake).

title: t19351: fix(pulse): capacity halving counts only host/provider pressure failures, not task outcomes
body:
## Task


`pulse_apply_provider_load_capacity_cap` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:556-578`) halves the worker target whenever `worker_terminal_failures >= 3` in the last 900 s. It counts every generic terminal failure from `worker-terminal-health.py`, including task outcomes that fewer concurrent workers cannot prevent:

- clean exit-0 runs whose objective reconciliation later failed them (`no_work`, `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`, `worker_merged_missing_linkage`, `worker_head_mismatch`, …);
- cross-runner claim coordination (`worker_ownership_lost`, `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed`);
- `merged_pr_reap`, and worker-reported blockers (`blocked`, `permission_required`).

Fix: the capacity cap counts only **pressure failures**, meaning failures that can show host or provider strain. Provider signals (rate limits, 5xx, exhausted service interruptions) stay unchanged. Current-state guardrails and launch pacing keep today's generic counts.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`pulse_apply_provider_load_capacity_cap` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:556-578`) halves the worker target whenever `worker_terminal_failures >= 3` in the last 900 s. It counts every generic terminal failure from `worker-terminal-health.py`, including task outcomes that fewer concurrent workers cannot prevent:

- clean exit-0 runs whose objective reconciliation later failed them (`no_work`, `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`, `worker_merged_missing_linkage`, `worker_head_mismatch`, …);
- cross-runner claim coordination (`worker_ownership_lost`, `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed`);
- `merged_pr_reap`, and worker-reported blockers (`blocked`, `permission_required`).

Fix: the capacity cap counts only **pressure failures**, meaning failures that can show host or provider strain. Provider signals (rate limits, 5xx, exhausted service interruptions) stay unchanged. Current-state guardrails and launch pacing keep today's generic counts.

## Why (measured 2026-11-24, one macOS runner, raw target 20)

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| `Dispatch_capacity` observations 05:00–23:15Z | 190 |
| Halved to 10 (`simultaneous_target_final=10`) | 40 (21%); 21 of 62 after the 16:25Z host recovery |
| Replay of the current rule from `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` + `objective-evidence.jsonl` | 35 halvings |
| Replay counting only pressure failures | 8 halvings |
| Launch opportunities lost, summed per observation as `max(0, raw − active) − max(0, final − active)` | 276 under the current rule, 78 counting pressure failures only |
| Counted failures after recovery (16:25–23:15Z) | `premature_exit` 9, clean exit 0 → objective `failed` 11, `worker_ownership_lost` 4, `local_error` 2, `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed` 1, `watchdog_stall_killed` 1, `merged_pr_reap` 1 |

Example: at 23:11:53Z a worker-exit refill found `simultaneous_target_raw=20 simultaneous_target_final=10 active_workers=11`, logged `Dispatch_max skipped: no available worker slots`, and launched nothing.

The halving was added for provider and load pressure (GH#23038 / PR #23061). GH#28873 already stopped reconciled successes from counting as failures. This change does the converse for failures that are task outcomes. Under `reference/throughput-throttling-policy.md`, halving concurrency for causes it cannot relieve is throttling without a root-cause fix.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/worker-terminal-health.py`:
  - Add an optional fifth argument, `--capacity-pressure`. In that mode, a counted failure is ignored when any of these holds:
    - `exit_code == 0`;
    - `result` is `blocked` or `permission_required`;
    - `failure_reason` is `worker_ownership_lost`, `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed` or `merged_pr_reap`.
  - Without the flag, output is unchanged. Invalid argument counts still print zeros and exit 2.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh` `_pulse_capacity_recent_health_counts`: pass `--capacity-pressure`.
  - Keep the fail-closed fallback (`0 3 0 0 0 0`).
  - Add a comment that `worker_terminal_failures` now reports pressure failures.
- Leave `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-current-state-guardrails.sh` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh` unchanged. They do not pass the flag.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-terminal-health.py`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`

## Acceptance

- Capacity counts ignore exit-0 `objective failed`, ownership-lost, `merged_pr_reap` and blocked rows. They still count `premature_exit`, `local_error`, `watchdog_stall_killed`, provider 5xx and rate limits.
- Guardrail and pacing counts are unchanged for the same fixture.
- The existing assertions in `test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh` and `test-worker-activity-helper.sh` still pass.
- After deploy: in a 6 h `pulse.log` window, the share of `Dispatch_capacity` lines with `simultaneous_target_final` < `simultaneous_target_raw` falls from about 21% toward the replayed ~4%, and `worker_terminal_failures` no longer includes clean-exit task outcomes.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh
rg -o 'simultaneous_target_raw=\d+ simultaneous_target_final=\d+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c
```

For #40108 (Phase 1 follow-up: capacity target halved by task-outcome failures).

body:
## What happened

`purelymail-helper.sh auth-results <addr> <secret> <subject-regex> [last-N]` printed `No message in the last 10 matched: ^Subject: DC accounts copy test` (and again with `'accounts copy test' 20` about 90 seconds later) for a message that was in the INBOX.

Evidence, same mailbox and same app password, read-only:

- `EXAMINE INBOX` returned `2 EXISTS`.
- Fetching each message on its own with curl (`imaps://imap.purelymail.com/INBOX;MAILINDEX=2;SECTION=HEADER.FIELDS%20(DATE%20FROM%20TO%20SUBJECT)`) returned `Subject: DC accounts copy test 0040 UTC` for message 2. Message 1 was Purelymail's welcome email.
- Related curl behaviour seen in the same session: a multi-message `FETCH 1:2 (BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS (...)])` sent with `-X` printed only the first message's literal. The newest matching message is found. Its `Authentication-Results` are then shown, or the command exits non-zero only because dkim, spf or dmarc failed.

title: purelymail-helper.sh: Sieve copy-to command (keep mail and send a copy), with Purelymail's STARTTLS quirk
body:
## Need

Mailboxes that should keep their mail and also send a copy elsewhere, such as a site's login mailbox copying to the owner's main address, have no helper command. The routing-rule API replaces delivery: a rule sends to its targets and doesn't keep the mail. The common setup is a webmail (Roundcube) filter, which the owner had to make by hand on the first site.

## Observed

On a second site this session needed the same filter. aidevops read the first mailbox's Sieve script over ManageSieve (read only), then wrote the identical script to the new mailbox. One-off tooling was invented for that: a small Python ManageSieve client using LISTSCRIPTS, GETSCRIPT, CHECKSCRIPT, PUTSCRIPT and SETACTIVE. The script, in Roundcube's format so it shows and stays editable under webmail Settings > Filters:

```sieve
require ["copy"];
# rule:[Copy to owner]
if true
{
	redirect :copy "owner@example.com";
}
```

Purelymail quirks found:

- `mailserver.purelymail.com:4190` does **not** re-send its capabilities after `STARTTLS`, as RFC 5804 says servers should. A client must send `CAPABILITY` itself, or it hangs.
- Username is the full address. `AUTHENTICATE "PLAIN"` works with the mailbox password or an app password with SIEVE scope.
- The script must be named `roundcube` to appear in webmail.

## Proposal

Add to `.agents/scripts/purelymail-helper.sh`:

- `sieve-list <addr> <secret-name>`: list scripts and print the active one (read only).
- `copy-to <addr> <secret-name> <target> [--dry-run]`: set the script above. Refuse if any script already exists; verify with GETSCRIPT.
- `copy-to-remove <addr> <secret-name> --yes`: deactivate and delete it.

The password goes through stdin or a `-K`-style config, never argv. Document it in `.agents/services/email/purelymail.md` under "Mailboxes and routing", including the STARTTLS quirk.

## Verify

On a test mailbox: run `copy-to`, send one message to it, and check it stays in the INBOX (IMAP) and arrives at the target. Then `copy-to-remove` and `sieve-list` should show no scripts.

title: t19352: fix(pulse): stale-assignment sweep discovers dead-worker claims with one search every normalize run
body:
## Task


The stale-assignment sweep is the only backstop that returns a dead worker's `status:in-progress`/`status:queued` claim to the queue. Dispatch candidates exclude active-status issues, so the reactive dedup recovery never sees them. Today the sweep almost never runs to completion:

- `normalize_active_issue_assignments` has one stage budget (about 140–160 s). `_normalize_reap_dead_stamps` uses 5–61 s of it.
- Five passes then rotate least-recently-started first (`pulse-issue-reconcile-rotation.sh`). Each pass lists every pulse repo (101 on this runner, 1–9 s per repo), so whichever pass runs first spends the remaining budget on listing and is killed.
- `unassign_stale` gets the first slot about once per five runs (about every 2 h), then is killed partway through the repos. The pending checkpoint-lease drain and the deferred claim-release replay (GH#37344) run only in that slot.

Fix: discover the runner's stale active claims with **one** REST search per normalize run. Run that sweep before the pass rotation on every run. Keep the per-repo pass as the fallback when search is unavailable.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

The stale-assignment sweep is the only backstop that returns a dead worker's `status:in-progress`/`status:queued` claim to the queue. Dispatch candidates exclude active-status issues, so the reactive dedup recovery never sees them. Today the sweep almost never runs to completion:

- `normalize_active_issue_assignments` has one stage budget (about 140–160 s). `_normalize_reap_dead_stamps` uses 5–61 s of it.
- Five passes then rotate least-recently-started first (`pulse-issue-reconcile-rotation.sh`). Each pass lists every pulse repo (101 on this runner, 1–9 s per repo), so whichever pass runs first spends the remaining budget on listing and is killed.
- `unassign_stale` gets the first slot about once per five runs (about every 2 h), then is killed partway through the repos. The pending checkpoint-lease drain and the deferred claim-release replay (GH#37344) run only in that slot.

Fix: discover the runner's stale active claims with **one** REST search per normalize run. Run that sweep before the pass rotation on every run. Keep the per-repo pass as the fallback when search is unavailable.

## Why (measured 2026-11-25, one macOS runner, 101 pulse repos)

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| `normalize_active_issue_assignments` runs since 2026-11-22 (`pulse-stage-timings.log`) | 43 |
| Runs killed by the stage watchdog (exit 124) | 42 |
| Pass substages completed in those runs | 2, both `reassign_self` |
| `Stale assignment scan:` summary lines in the current `pulse.log` | 0 |
| `Deferred claim releases:` drains in 24 normalize runs | 5, one retaining 10 releases |
| One `search/issues` call for this runner's stale active claims, fleet-wide | about 1 s, 5 results |

Live examples on a private managed repo, both with dead dispatch PIDs and still `status:in-progress`:

- One claim's worker exited about 50 s after launch with `worker_ownership_lost`, after a single failed `gh issue view` (`WORKER_OWNERSHIP_UNKNOWN`, rc=2). Labels stayed put for 1.8 h.
- One parent's partial PR merged and its terminal lease was written. The issue still showed `status:in-progress` 2.5 h later.

Both are exactly the cases the sweep exists to recover. The sweep is starved, so each such claim keeps a queue item unavailable for hours. That is lost around-the-clock throughput (GH#40108). GH#40204 (PR #40207) added orphaned self-claim recovery inside this same sweep, so it is starved too.

Prior partial fixes (GH#37362 shared listing, GH#37565 reaper wall-clock bound, GH#37568 per-pass repo cursor) reduced cost but kept discovery at O(repos), so the stage still times out every run.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`
  - Extract the per-candidate body of `_normalize_unassign_stale` (skip gate, GH#40204 orphan hook, audited `CLAIM_RELEASED` then reset) into a helper, so the per-repo pass and the search pass share one code path. Keep the guards unchanged.
  - Add search-driven discovery. Issue one `gh api -X GET search/issues` with `is:issue is:open assignee:<runner> label:"status:in-progress","status:queued" updated:<cutoff>`, sorted by `updated` ascending, `per_page=100`. Keep only slugs that `repos.json` lists as pulse repos (not `local_only`) and that `repo_allows_pulse_write_actions` permits. Cap candidates per run, default 30, oldest first.
  - Before any API read, skip a candidate when `_normalize_stale_session_leader_live` shows a live same-device registered worker. Today such a candidate is always skipped; the new check only avoids the network reads.
  - The search sweep returns non-zero when search fails, when `incomplete_results` is true, or when results reach `per_page`. The caller then keeps the per-repo pass for that run.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` `normalize_active_issue_assignments`
  - After `_normalize_reap_dead_stamps` and runner resolution, run the checkpoint-lease drain, the deferred claim-release replay and the search sweep on every run, with substage timing.
  - In the rotation, the `unassign_stale` case does nothing when the search sweep succeeded this run. Otherwise it runs today's three calls unchanged.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-search.sh`

## Acceptance

- One normalize run makes exactly one `search/issues` call for stale discovery. Each candidate goes through the same skip gate and audited reset as the per-repo pass.
- A candidate with a live same-device session leader makes no GitHub call.
- When search fails, is incomplete or hits the page limit, the per-repo `unassign_stale` pass still runs in the rotation.
- `test-issue-reconcile.sh`, `test-pulse-issue-reconcile-orphaned-self-claim.sh` and `test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-open-pr.sh` still pass.
- After deploy, every normalize run logs a `Stale assignment scan (search):` summary in `pulse.log`. A dead-PID active claim is released within one or two normalize runs (about 25–50 min), not hours.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-search.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile-orphaned-self-claim.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-open-pr.sh
rg -c 'Stale assignment scan \(search\):' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
```

For #40108 (Phase 1 follow-up: active claims of dead workers stay unavailable for hours because the stale sweep is starved).

## What

### Files Scope

title: fix(pulse-merge): trust scoped services-sync worker briefs at the worker-briefed gate
body:
## What

Let worker PRs that implement the scheduled site services-sync briefs merge through the existing worker-briefed gate. Bind trust to the generator's exact issue shape and its two-file scope, the same way the OpenCode pin-canary (GH#35752) and starter-sync (GH#37289) exceptions are bound. Do not add a broad `github-actions[bot]` exception.

## Why

The site repository's services-sync workflow files `origin:worker` + `auto-dispatch` issues as `github-actions[bot]` (`author_association=CONTRIBUTOR`). The body carries `<!-- aidevops:generator=services-sync-check -->`, and the title has the form `Sync site services list with upstream aidevops (<7-char sha>)`. Example: marcusquinn/aidevops.sh#214.

Its worker PR marcusquinn/aidevops.sh#219 has been green since 2026-11-19. It changes one line pair in `data/services-sync.json`, and review-bot returns `PASS_RATE_LIMITED`. It still cannot merge:

- `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr 219 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops.sh` shows 150+ `pm-wb-not-owner` skips (`pulse-merge.sh:1544`).
- A supervisor run of `full-loop-helper.sh merge 219 marcusquinn/aidevops.sh --squash` on 2026-11-25 failed with: `Merge blocked by t2449: linked issue #214 author_association=CONTRIBUTOR ... no cryptographic approval signature found`.

Each upstream services change produces another PR that stalls the same way, until a maintainer merges it by hand or signs an approval.

## Reproducer

1. `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr 219 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops.sh`. Expect `pm-wb-not-owner` as the last pulse decision.
2. `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh merge 219 marcusquinn/aidevops.sh --squash`. Expect `Merge blocked by t2449: linked issue #214 author_association=CONTRIBUTOR`.
3. `gh issue view 214 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops.sh --json author`. Expect `github-actions[bot]`.

## How

- Add `_is_trusted_services_sync_issue_pr` to `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh`. Model it on `_is_trusted_starter_sync_issue_pr` (same file, around lines 181-270) and mark it `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
  - The issue author must be exactly `github-actions[bot]` with `user.type == Bot`.
  - The title must match `^Sync site services list with upstream aidevops \([0-9a-f]{7}\)$`.
  - The issue must carry `origin:worker`, and its body must contain the `aidevops:generator=services-sync-check` marker.
  - Every changed PR file must be `index.html` or `data/services-sync.json`, with 1-2 files, no renames, and a full file list. Any API error fails closed.
- Call it from `_worker_briefed_trust_check` next to the canary and starter-sync alternatives, before crypto approval.
- Apply the same predicate in the full-loop merge authority path (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh`, the t2449 check). Interactive and supervisor merges must agree. `tests/test-worker-briefed-trust-parity.sh` guards that parity.
- Every other merge gate stays: required checks, reviews, review-bot and NMR.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-briefed-trust-parity.sh`

## Verification

- Run the live predicate read-only: marcusquinn/aidevops.sh#219 with #214 should come back trusted. The same issue paired with a PR that touches any other file should be rejected. A non-bot issue with the same title should be rejected.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-briefed-trust-parity.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-issue-sync-authority.sh` pass. ShellCheck is clean.
- After deploy, the next pulse merge pass merges marcusquinn/aidevops.sh#219, or the PR is merged by hand if it has gone stale.

## Notes

- If the generator also needs to edit `index.html` count claims, it does so within the same two-file scope. Bound it no wider.
- Precedents: GH#35795 (pin-canary), starter-sync GH#37289/GH#39910.

title: t19354: fix: report-token-use classifies worktree-based headless workers as interactive
body:
Session-kind split misattributes pulse worker spend in linked worktrees to interactive sessions

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`report-token-use-helper.py` classifies pulse-dispatched headless workers as `interactive`, so the session-type split hides where most spend goes.

## Evidence

A 14-day local report (2026-11-25) put 1,684 sessions and $3,342 of cost from 2026-11-21 onwards under "Interactive", and only 136 sessions and $2 under "Headless worker". About 1,420 of those "interactive" rows are `opencode run` workers. Their titles look like `Issue #N: ...` and their directories are pulse-created linked worktrees named `<repo>-feature-auto-<timestamp>-gh<N>` under the worktree base dir. Running `ps` showed 16 live `opencode run --title Issue ...` processes in those directories. Only the throwaway temp-dir sessions match the current rule.

## Why

`_session_kind_for_group` (`.agents/scripts/report-token-use-helper.py:364`) only matches `/tmp/opencode`-style directories. Workers dispatched into linked worktrees (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`, `worktree-helper-add.sh` `feature/auto-*` naming) never match that rule.

## How

1. Prefer an authoritative signal: join on the session IDs that `headless-runtime-helper.sh` records (`METRICS_FILE` / `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_METRICS_FILE`, `session_id` field around line 732-743), or on the `store_session_id` state under `STATE_DIR`.
2. Fall back to a directory heuristic: a worktree basename matching `-feature-auto-\d{8}-\d{6}-gh\d+` counts as `headless_worker`.
3. Keep the existing temp-dir rule. Record the signal used in a `session_kind_provenance` JSON field, following the existing `*_provenance` fields.
4. Optional: add a per-repository/per-directory cost table to the report, because spend is dominated by one repo's worker fleet and the report has no repo dimension today.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/report-token-use-helper.py`
- `.agents/scripts/report_token_use_render.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-report-token-use-helper.sh`

## Reference pattern

Model on the existing `cost_provenance` / `lineage_provenance` fields in `.agents/scripts/report-token-use-helper.py` for recording which signal set a derived value.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `report-token-use-helper.sh report --since 3d` lists `feature-auto` worktree worker sessions as "Headless worker".
- [ ] Genuine interactive sessions (canonical repo dirs, non-auto worktrees) stay "Interactive".

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-report-token-use-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/report-token-use-helper.sh report --since 3d
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: macos-account-keychain-recovery.md: require absolute keychain paths, add stuck-SecurityAgent recovery and Keychain Access fallback
body:
## Problem

`tools/security/macos-account-keychain-recovery.md` section 3 tells the user to copy a recovered keychain to a folder as `login.keychain-db` and run `security unlock-keychain <folder>/login.keychain-db`. In a real recovery session:

1. A follow-up command passed the keychain as a bare/relative name. `security` resolves bare keychain names against `~/Library/Keychains/`, so the command targeted the **live** login keychain, not the recovered copy. The resulting prompts asked for the live keychain while the user entered the old password.
2. With the live keychain locked, background `gh` credential lookups (`security find-generic-password -s gh:github.com -wa`) queued 50+ processes. That left a SecurityAgent dialog that Cancel/OK would not dismiss (GH#37232 pattern).
3. The item-level ACL dialog ("allow security to access item X") rejected both known passwords for the recovered copy, even after `unlock-keychain` succeeded.

## What worked

- Clear the queue: kill the pending `security find-generic-password` PIDs. If the dialog persists, `kill -9` the SecurityAgent PID (SIGTERM was ignored). launchd respawns it.
- Unlock the live keychain with a **full path**: `security unlock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db`.
- Read the item in the GUI instead of the CLI: add the recovered copy with `security list-keychains -d user -s <live> <copy>`, relaunch Keychain Access, unlock the copy, open the item, tick "Show password", copy, then paste into the target app. Remove the copy from the search list afterwards.

## Requested change

Update section 3 (and the agent-effects bullet near line 67) of `.agents/tools/security/macos-account-keychain-recovery.md`:
- Always pass absolute keychain paths to `security`; never bare names.
- Add the stuck-dialog recovery steps above.
- Prefer the Keychain Access "Show password" route when the CLI item-ACL prompt rejects the password.

## Verification

Read-through review of the updated doc; `markdownlint` clean; no new instructions duplicated elsewhere (`rg -n "unlock-keychain" .agents/`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/security/macos-account-keychain-recovery.md`

title: t19356: Headless workers: prompt-cache keep-warm during long tool calls + require repeated Sonnet failure before Opus escalation
body:
## Task


Cut avoidable Anthropic token use in headless workers without reducing throughput:

1. **Prompt-cache keep-warm during long tool calls.** Anthropic's default 5-minute cache expires while a bash call runs longer than 5 minutes. The next request then re-writes the whole 150-250k-token context.
2. **Opus escalation needs repeated failures.** `tier:standard` → `tier:thinking` (Opus) currently fires on the first `overwhelmed` failure. Most of these failures are `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`. Opus should be used only after Sonnet fails more than once.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs`: after each successful authenticated request, remember its transformed body and headers per host session. While a tool call for that session is still running (tracked by tool hooks), replay the request with `max_tokens: 1` every ~270s, up to a cap (default 60 min). The replay only refreshes the cache TTL. Fail-open. Opt-out env: `AIDEVOPS_CACHE_KEEPALIVE=0`.
- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cache-keepalive.mjs`: the scheduler with injectable timers and fetch, so it can be tested.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`: wire `tool.execute.before/after` into the keep-alive tracker.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` `escalate_issue_tier`: escalation into `tier:thinking` requires `failure_count >= ESCALATION_THINKING_MIN_FAILURES` (default 2). `simple → standard` is unchanged. Use a `>=` threshold; the label state keeps it idempotent. The body-gate comment is posted only once, at the exact threshold.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/context-efficiency.md`: guidance on long tool waits and cache TTL. Model escalation policy goes in the routing docs.

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cache-keepalive.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-cache-keepalive.mjs
- .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-tier-routing.sh
- .agents/reference/context-efficiency.md

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Cut avoidable Anthropic token use in headless workers without reducing throughput:

1. **Prompt-cache keep-warm during long tool calls.** Anthropic's default 5-minute cache expires while a bash call runs longer than 5 minutes. The next request then re-writes the whole 150-250k-token context.
2. **Opus escalation needs repeated failures.** `tier:standard` → `tier:thinking` (Opus) currently fires on the first `overwhelmed` failure. Most of these failures are `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`. Opus should be used only after Sonnet fails more than once.

## Why (evidence, local observability DB, award workers 2026-11-22..25)

- 437.7M cache-write tokens across 1,296 award worker sessions.
- 130.9M of them (29.9%) followed a gap of 5-60 min since the previous request started (886 events). Nearly all were single long tool calls (gap 5-10 min: 774 events).
- 1,150 bash calls ran longer than 280s:
  - `award-enrichment-beta-lock.ts run`: 541 calls, median 354s.
  - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: 123 calls, median 369s.
  - lane claim/publish: about 80 calls, about 330s.
  - `full-loop-helper.sh merge`: about 60 calls, 300s.
- In example session ses_deff57…, every long call (474-662s) was followed by `cache_read=11599` (tools+system only) and `cache_write` of 143-200k.
- The `cache-stability` monitor showed no byte changes for these requests, so prefix churn is not the cause. TTL expiry is.
- Simulating a 1h TTL on every write gave +5.9% net cost, so a blanket 1h TTL is rejected. A keep-warm read costs about 0.1x of the context per 4.5 minutes, against a 1.25x re-write.
- Escalations since Nov 18: 101 of about 140 logged escalation comments were `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`, classified `overwhelmed` with threshold 1.

## Acceptance criteria

- After deploy, award workers show far fewer `cache_read≈11.6k` re-writes after long tool calls (rerun `ttl_sim`-style analysis on llm-requests.db).
- A `tier:standard` issue with one `overwhelmed` failure stays standard; with two failures it escalates to `tier:thinking`.
- Existing plugin and shell tests pass; ShellCheck is clean.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-tier-routing.sh`

title: pulse-routines: BSD chmod rejects 'chmod <mode> --', so routine output is never saved on macOS
body:
## Problem

On macOS every script routine's output is discarded since GH#40174. `_routine_save_output` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:613-614` runs `chmod 700 -- "$output_dir"` and `chmod 600 -- "$output_file"`. BSD `chmod` (macOS) treats a `--` that follows the mode as a file operand. It fails with `chmod: --: No such file or directory`, so the `&&` chain short-circuits, `pulse.log` records `routine <id>: output_saved=false`, and line 626 deletes the temp output.

## Evidence (macOS 26, aidevops v3.39.278)

- `chmod 600 -- <file>` prints `chmod: --: No such file or directory`. `chmod -- 600 <file>` succeeds silently.
- On one maintainer Mac, `pulse.log` has 116 `output_saved=false` lines and 0 `output saved path=` lines since the GH#40174 deploy.
- The per-routine logs `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log.routine-<id>.log` and `pulse-routines-tick.log.routine-<id>.log` contain only repeated `chmod: --: No such file or directory` lines. No routine run output can be inspected after the fact, which hides routine failures.

## Fix

Put `--` before the mode (`chmod -- 700 "$output_dir"`, `chmod -- 600 "$output_file"`), which BSD and GNU both accept. Alternatively drop `--`, since both paths are absolute under `$HOME`. Grep the other framework scripts for `chmod <mode> --` and fix any other occurrences the same way.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- On macOS, run one script routine through the pulse tick. Confirm `pulse.log` records `output saved path=~/.aidevops/logs/routines/<id>.log` and that the file exists with mode 600 in a 700 directory.
- Repeat on Linux (GNU coreutils) to confirm no regression.

title: Headless workers pause on external_directory walls for /dev, /proc and their own temp roots; stale walls accumulate
body:
## Problem

Headless workers in a managed project repo keep pausing on "Maintainer permission required" for `external_directory` reads of system pseudo-paths and their own temp directories. The issue then stays `status:blocked` with `needs-maintainer-permissions` until a maintainer signs a withdrawal with sudo. Meanwhile it occupies a per-URL issue slot and counts toward the project's open-issue fuse, which stops new work from being filed.

## Evidence (one managed project repo, 2026-11-25)

Nine open issues are held by stale requests whose worker sessions ended 5 to 12 days ago:

- `/dev/*`: four requests (2026-11-15 to 2026-11-20)
- `/proc/*`: two requests (2026-11-14 and 2026-11-16)
- `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/*` or a subdirectory: two requests
- `~/.aidevops-private/tmp/*`: one request
- `~/*`: one request (broad; must stay held)

Three of these issues then passed through the project's three automatic retries and were marked unavailable, although their award sources were never tested.

## Expected

- Reads of `/dev/null`, `/dev/stdin|stdout|stderr`, `/dev/fd/*` and the worker's own temp roots under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/` should not trigger an interactive permission wall in headless sessions. For example, allow them in the generated OpenCode permission config, or have the worker brief route temp writes through the existing workspace paths.
- `/proc/*` on Linux (for example memory probes) needs an explicit decision: allow read-only access to `/proc/self/*` and `/proc/meminfo`, or keep it walled.
- Broad requests (`~/*`) stay held, as now.
- Consider auto-withdrawing, or at least surfacing in the pulse, requests whose session has ended. The current rule needs a signed decision for every request, and stale walls accumulate unseen.

Start from the headless worker permission profile in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-worker-permissions.mjs` and the broker that raises the wall (`permission-broker.mjs`, `permission-broker-read-target.mjs`). Stale-request handling lives in `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`. Confirm the exact generation path before editing; extend the existing tests in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs` and `test-worker-permission-grant.mjs`.

### Files Scope

<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=gh40255-integration -->
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-worker-permission-grant.mjs`

Brief repaired: the config hook calls managed-directory registration followed by signed-grant registration; baseline runtime permissions need an explicit hook call, independent of grants. The broker dispatches its bounded read-target classifier through both permission APIs. The existing grant suite verifies generated worker rules. Collision discovery found no competing PR or claim on these paths. Verify with the existing broker, grant and managed-directory Node suites plus the worker-permission-helper shell suite. Keep /proc walled and retain signed withdrawal for stale requests; no blanket /dev, home or private-temp grant.
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-worker-permissions.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-read-target.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-permission-helper.sh`

## Verification

- Run a headless worker that executes `cmd 2>/dev/null` and writes under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/` and confirm no permission request is raised.
- Confirm a `~/*` read still raises a request.
- Existing permission broker/helper tests per `reference/dispatch-blockers.md`.
