title: t19357: feat(worktree): clone pnpm workspace node_modules (root + members) into fresh worktrees instead of full install
body:
## Task


Make a fresh linked worktree of a pnpm workspace monorepo ready to run its tests without a full `pnpm install`. That means restoring the root `node_modules` and each workspace member's `node_modules` (`packages/*`, `apps/*`). Do it with copy-on-write clones on APFS (`cp -c` / clonefile) or reflink on Linux, gated by the existing lockfile identity checks.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make a fresh linked worktree of a pnpm workspace monorepo ready to run its tests without a full `pnpm install`. That means restoring the root `node_modules` and each workspace member's `node_modules` (`packages/*`, `apps/*`). Do it with copy-on-write clones on APFS (`cp -c` / clonefile) or reflink on Linux, gated by the existing lockfile identity checks.

## Why

In a private pnpm monorepo, headless workers ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` in every fresh worktree. Over 3 days that was 123 runs, median 369s. The prompt cache also expires during the wait, so each install forces a context re-write. That repo's AGENTS.md tells workers that "the framework's copy of node_modules ... misses packages/*".

Code-reading evidence (line numbers from `main` at the time of filing):

- `_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py:160-190` does a validated byte copy through memory, not a clone.
- `worktree-dependency-provision.py:58-59,83` hard-caps the copy at 64 MiB and 20,000 entries. A pnpm monorepo's `node_modules` is far larger. `worktree-helper-add.sh:439-458,503-506` then rejects it with `source-exceeds-budget`.
- `worktree-helper-add.sh:599` and `pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh:141-145` only try directories that have their own lockfile. `_worktree_dependency_identity.py:150-155` (`matching_lock`) requires the lockfile in the package directory. Workspace members whose lock lives at the root are skipped, and the comment at `pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh:142-143` says so.
- `WORKTREE_NODE_MODULES_RESTORE_MAX_DIRS:=2` (`worktree-helper-add.sh:39`) limits the attempt to two directories.
- pnpm workspace symlinks that point at `../../packages/*` would fail the `escaping-package-root` check in `_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py:106-113`.
- The headless path calls `_dlw_restore_worktree_deps` in `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` around lines 575 and 665, which reaches the same `_provision_worktree_node_modules`. Rejections are only logged as "Dependency provisioning unavailable".

## How

1. Add a pnpm workspace mode.
   - Detect it from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` plus a root `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
   - Verify identity once against the root lock: the source and worktree `pnpm-lock.yaml` must be byte-identical, and the root `node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml` must match.
   - Then restore root `node_modules` and every member `node_modules` listed by the workspace globs.
2. Use a copy-on-write clone for this mode. On macOS: `cp -cR` with clonefile; on Linux: `cp -a --reflink=auto`. Skip the 64 MiB byte budget, because a clone costs no data copy. Keep the byte-copy path as the fallback when clone is unsupported.
3. Allow relative symlinks inside the worktree root that point at workspace members. Keep rejecting links that escape the worktree.
4. Wire the mode into both the interactive (`worktree-helper-add.sh`) and headless (`pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh`) restore paths. Log one line per restore with the outcome and elapsed time.
5. If identity differs, fall back to the existing behaviour. That is either the owner-approved install, or the worker running `pnpm install`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_identity.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-dependency-provision.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_manifest.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_payload.py`

Brief repaired: terminal Qlty regression at PR #40260 head 9b1a0c965601 requires cohesive manifest-parsing and descriptor-payload modules rather than growing the identity and snapshot files. The separately assigned CI repair produced commit 97a5fa949392a75876bf12dcda8a240a7bd09dfb; these two adjacent implementation paths are recorded before the original executor adopts that repair. No explicit exclusions, permissions or security guarantees are widened. Verified no other PR/claim collision for the added paths after the repair executor released its push. Verify with python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py, bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-js-dependency-bootstrap.sh, and the pinned Qlty regression helper against the existing PR base.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a pnpm workspace with identical lockfiles, a new worktree gets working root and member `node_modules`, so `pnpm exec tsx --version` runs from a member directory. No install runs.
- [ ] A lockfile mismatch falls back to the current behaviour and logs the reason.
- [ ] Symlinks that escape the worktree are still rejected.
- [ ] Restore time on APFS for a large monorepo is reported in the log, in seconds.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-js-dependency-bootstrap.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-deps.sh`
- Manual check: create a worktree of any local pnpm workspace repo, then check the provisioning log line and run a member-package command.

title: t19358: Add prompt-cache keep-alive to the OpenCode v2 provider-auth adapter
body:
## Task


Give OpenCode v2 the prompt-cache keep-alive that PR #40256 added for v1, so long tool calls stop forcing full cache rebuilds there too.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Give OpenCode v2 the prompt-cache keep-alive that PR #40256 added for v1, so long tool calls stop forcing full cache rebuilds there too.

## Why

On v1, PR #40256 records each completed agent request. While a tool runs longer than the 5-minute cache TTL, it re-sends that request with `max_tokens: 1`. In one worker fleet, about 29.9% of cache writes followed 5–60 minute gaps; this removes them.

The v2 adapter does not record requests, so v2 sessions still pay those rebuilds. OpenCode v1 is the active host today, so this is not urgent. Without it, the saving disappears when hosts move to v2.

## Dependency

Blocked by #40251: PR #40256 adds `cache-keepalive.mjs` and the v1 wiring. Start only after that PR has merged to `main`. A worker that finds `cache-keepalive.mjs` missing should stop as blocked rather than recreate it.

## How

- Files to modify:
  - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-provider-auth.mjs`: in `createHttpResponseHook`, after a 2xx Anthropic response, call `cacheKeepalive.recordRequest(event.sessionID, <send context>, <pre-transform body>, status)`.
  - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`: wire tool start/finish to `cacheKeepalive.toolStarted` / `toolFinished`, matching `index.mjs` (`rg -n "cacheKeepalive" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`).
  - `cache-keepalive.mjs` and `provider-auth.mjs` are in scope only to export or share an existing helper with v2, such as a host-neutral send builder. Do not change v1 behaviour.
- Reference pattern:
  - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs`: see `sendCacheKeepalive` and the `cacheKeepalive.recordRequest(` call. Refreshes re-run the same body transforms and auth headers as the real request.
  - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cache-keepalive.mjs`: `createCacheKeepalive({ send })` is host-neutral. Reuse it rather than duplicating the scheduler.
- Constraint: v2 uses request/response hooks, not a fetch wrapper. The `send` callback must issue its own `fetch` with a freshly resolved access token. Reuse `anthropicRequest()` / `transformedBody()` so the refresh body matches the cached prefix byte for byte. Fail open on any error.
- Hazard: the rotation probe loads plugin modules in an isolated VM with an allowlist (`.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs`). If v2 imports a new module, keep `tests/test-oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs` green.
- Unknown: the v2 tool-lifecycle hook names. Confirm them from `v2.mjs` and the `@opencode-ai/plugin` v2 types before wiring.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-provider-auth.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cache-keepalive.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-cache-keepalive.mjs`

## Acceptance

- `node --test tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs tests/test-cache-keepalive.mjs tests/test-oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs tests/test-provider-auth-cch.mjs` passes, run from `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`.
- New v2 coverage (positive): a recorded 2xx request plus a running tool triggers one refresh with `max_tokens: 1`.
- New v2 coverage (negative): no refresh after the tool finishes, after a non-2xx response, or when `AIDEVOPS_CACHE_KEEPALIVE=0`.
- Regression: existing v1 keep-alive tests pass unchanged.
- If a v2 host is available, check the logs: a `[aidevops] cache-keepalive: ... cache_read=<N> cache_write=0` line should appear during a tool call longer than 4 minutes.

title: t19359: fix(disk-capacity): count APFS purgeable capacity toward the worktree percentage floor on macOS
body:
## Task


Count macOS APFS "important usage" capacity toward the worktree/dispatch percentage floor in `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh`, so space that macOS holds as purgeable (Time Machine local snapshots, purgeable caches) and reclaims on demand no longer idles every worker slot.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Count macOS APFS "important usage" capacity toward the worktree/dispatch percentage floor in `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh`, so space that macOS holds as purgeable (Time Machine local snapshots, purgeable caches) and reclaims on demand no longer idles every worker slot.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25 on a 3.6 TiB APFS volume: `df` reported 47.4 GiB available (1%), below the 50 GiB capped 5% floor, so every dispatch attempt logged `disk space critical (reason=below-minimum-percent …)` (67+ blocks in one window) and worker occupancy fell to zero. Deleting ~12 GiB of disposable temp trees freed nothing visible because two purgeable Time Machine local snapshots (2026-11-16, 2026-11-24) pin the blocks; finished-worktree cleanup reports `reclaimed_mib=0` for the same reason. At the same moment `NSURLVolumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey` reported 666.8 GB: macOS guarantees that capacity to user-initiated writes and purges the snapshots itself when it is needed. GH#38026 capped the floor and added a read-only advisory, but the gate still reads raw `df` and blocks until a human thins backups — the user-attention dependency aidevops exists to remove.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh`: add a read-only Darwin probe (`osascript -l JavaScript`, Foundation `NSURL` resource value `NSURLVolumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey`, path passed as argv, bounded by the existing `timeout_sec`/`timeout`/`gtimeout` pattern used by `aidevops_disk_capacity_reclaim_hint`). Run it only when raw `df` headroom is below the percentage floor. Admit when important-usage capacity meets the floor; keep the absolute 5 GiB minimum and quota checks on raw numbers so ENOSPC protection is unchanged. `AIDEVOPS_DISK_COUNT_PURGEABLE=0` restores the raw-only policy. Never thin, delete or modify snapshots.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`: log once per pulse process when admission relied on purgeable capacity (raw vs important KB) so the decision is observable.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh`: stub `uname`/`osascript` so the suite stays deterministic on macOS hosts and covers credit-admits, credit-insufficient, opt-out, and non-Darwin cases.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh`

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh` passes on macOS and Linux.
- ShellCheck clean for the touched scripts.
- On a Darwin host whose raw `df` headroom is below the floor but important-usage capacity is above it, `aidevops_worktree_capacity_check` returns 0 and Pulse logs the purgeable-admission line; with `AIDEVOPS_DISK_COUNT_PURGEABLE=0` it returns 1 `below-minimum-percent`.
- Raw headroom below 5 GiB still blocks regardless of purgeable capacity.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh
rg -n 'purgeable' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -n 3
```

title: t19360: fix(complexity-scan): reap leaked complexity-scan-tree clones and clean up on interruption
body:
## Task


Stop the weekly complexity scan from leaking `complexity-scan-tree.XXXXXX` clones under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`, and reap clones that earlier interrupted scans already left behind.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop the weekly complexity scan from leaking `complexity-scan-tree.XXXXXX` clones under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`, and reap clones that earlier interrupted scans already left behind.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25: 41 leaked scan trees (2026-10-22 … 2026-11-25), ~9.3 GiB counted once across the set, in a temp directory with ~38,600 top-level entries and no sweeper. Each tree is a `git clone --local` plus a full origin/main checkout made by `_complexity_scan_pull_latest` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh:821`). Only `run_weekly_complexity_scan` removes it (`.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh:726-728`), after `_run_weekly_complexity_scan_in` returns, so any interrupted scan leaks the tree: a killed `complexity-scan-runner.sh run`, a pulse stage timeout, or a reboot. One live runner had been inside a 3-hour-old tree for 1h47m. On a host whose disk gate was already blocking dispatch, the leak was a direct cost.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh` `run_weekly_complexity_scan`: guarantee removal on interruption. Use a RETURN/EXIT/INT/TERM-safe cleanup scoped to this function, and restore any previous trap. Model it on `_release_lock` in `.agents/scripts/complexity-scan-runner.sh:118-146`. Never remove the canonical `aidevops_path`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh` `_complexity_scan_pull_latest`: before `mktemp`, reap direct children of the temp base that match `complexity-scan-tree.??????`. Reap a directory only when it is a real directory (not a symlink), older than 24 h (env override `AIDEVOPS_COMPLEXITY_SCAN_TREE_MAX_AGE_HOURS`), and has no process cwd inside it (`lsof -n -Fn -d cwd` when available; skip reaping when `lsof` is missing). Log one summary line `Complexity scan: reaped N stale scan tree(s)` to `$LOGFILE`.
- Reference implementation of the same safety checks (one-off, already run on the reporting host): validate-then-remove by name pattern, age, cwd-in-use and origin remote, with dry-run by default.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-complexity-scan.sh`

## Acceptance

- An interrupted scan (simulate by sending TERM to the subshell running `_run_weekly_complexity_scan_in`) leaves no `complexity-scan-tree.*` directory behind.
- Stale trees older than the threshold are removed on the next scan; trees younger than it, or with a live cwd inside, are kept.
- The canonical repo path is never removed (the existing non-git in-place path keeps working).
- ShellCheck clean; `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-complexity-scan.sh` passes.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-complexity-scan.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-orchestration.sh
fd --max-depth 1 -t d -g 'complexity-scan-tree.*' ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp
```

title: t19361: fix(opencode-db-archive): support the session_inbox schema generation so the 92 GB interactive DB is archived and event-expired
body:
## Task


Teach the OpenCode DB archive, event-expiry, retention and restore paths the current OpenCode session-schema generation. The generation is the one introduced by migrations `20260812181746_session_inbox` … `20260910120000_clear_v1_session_permission`. Today every run against it fails closed with rc=3, so the largest active DB is never archived or event-expired.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Teach the OpenCode DB archive, event-expiry, retention and restore paths the current OpenCode session-schema generation. The generation is the one introduced by migrations `20260812181746_session_inbox` … `20260910120000_clear_v1_session_permission`. Today every run against it fails closed with rc=3, so the largest active DB is never archived or event-expired.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-25 (archive log, 50 consecutive runs): the interactive aidevops DB under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-interactive/project-aidevops-<hash>/opencode/opencode.db` is 92 GB (22.5 M pages, 4,553 sessions, 0 free pages). Every inventory logs:

`Unsupported or unavailable OpenCode session schema: table=session_input actual_columns=[missing] … reason=column-mismatch; active data was left untouched.` → `rc=3`.

The runtime that owns it (OpenCode 1.19.6, the current interactive build) migrated the schema as follows:

- dropped `session_input` and `session_context_epoch`;
- added `session_inbox(id,session_id,type,payload,delivery,enqueued_seq,time_created)`, `session_pending(id,session_id,type,data,delivery,admitted_seq,time_created)`, `instruction_entry(session_id,key,value,removed,time_created,time_updated)`, `instruction_state(session_id,epoch_start,through_seq,initial_values,current_values)`, `instruction_blob(hash,value)`, `session_v2(...)` (no `session_id` column), `kv`, `worktree`;
- added a `created` column to `event` (`id,aggregate_id,seq,type,data,created`).

`session`, `message`, `part`, `todo`, `session_share`, `session_message` and `event_sequence` keep their supported column sets. All of the new session-scoped tables are currently empty, so the data lives in tables the helper already moves. Because `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-worker-events.sh:130` validates the schema first, the GH#38491/GH#38630 event-expiry pass also never runs here. That pass is what kept the `event` table from regrowing to ~78 GB on older DBs. As more DBs open under the current runtime, every one will stop being maintained.

## How

Keep the fail-closed contract for unknown generations; add this generation as a known one.

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh` (`opencode_archive_table_schema_supported`, `opencode_archive_schema_supported` ~L190-289): add supported column sets for `session_inbox`, `session_pending`, `instruction_entry`, `instruction_state`, and the `event` set with `created`. Make `session_input`/`session_context_epoch` optional when the session-inbox generation is detected (for example `session_inbox` exists). Extend the `unknown-session-table` allowlist with the four new `session_id` tables. Keep `instruction_blob`, `kv`, `worktree` and `session_v2` out of the session-scoped set: they have no `session_id` column, so the existing checks never treat them as session-scoped.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-schema.sh` (`_archive_session_schema_sql` ~L161-215, `_archive_migrate_schema_columns`): create the new session-scoped tables in the archive DB and migrate `event.created`.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh` (count/copy/delete blocks around L1199-1245, L1300, L1411-1530, L1457): copy and delete rows of the new session-scoped tables with their session, using the existing `has_session_input_table` optional-table pattern.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-retention.sh` (~L151-168) and `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-restore.sh` (~L37): include the new tables in retention deletes and restore copies.
- Never write to an active DB that fails validation. Keep transactional batches, idle/heartbeat gating and integrity checks unchanged.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-schema.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-retention.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-restore.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`

## Acceptance

- A fixture DB with the new generation's schema (build it from the column lists above, or from `sqlite3 -readonly <db> .schema` on a host DB; never copy production data) passes validation. Inactive sessions archive with message/part/event rows and any `session_inbox`/`session_pending`/`instruction_*` rows. Restore round-trips them.
- The legacy generation (with `session_input`/`session_context_epoch`) still validates and archives as before.
- A DB with an additional unknown `session_id` table still fails closed with rc=3 and leaves data untouched.
- On the reporting host, the next scheduled run logs a non-3 outcome for the interactive aidevops DB, and the event-expiry pass runs against it.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-db-safety-lib.sh .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive*.sh
rg -n 'project-aidevops-.*rc=' ~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-db-archive.log | tail -n 3
```

## Related

- GH#35902 (V2 parity tracker; its "DB archive path and schema" item covers the V2 data dir, while this is the current V1 runtime's schema)
- GH#38491, GH#38630 (event expiry)

</details>

title: Storage lifecycle: worker-built Docker images and build cache have no owner (175 GB observed); escalate npm cache advisory under low disk
body:
## Problem

Worker test/verification runs build Docker images (names like `<app>-gh<N>:candidate`, `opendesk-gh45:verify`, `netbird-smoke:<tag>`) and accumulate BuildKit cache. No aidevops store owns their lifecycle, and `aidevops cleanup` does not report them.

Observed on one macOS install (OrbStack), with the system disk at 99%:

- `docker system df`: 231 images (22 active), 113.5 GB, 80 GB reclaimable. Build cache: 2364 entries, 107.5 GB, 0 active. 367 local volumes, 57.8 GB, 48 GB reclaimable.
- The OrbStack disk image takes 175 GB on the host.
- Most images are per-issue worker artefacts that are 1–5 weeks old.

The npm cache (`~/.npm/_cacache`) reached 387 GB on the same machine. `aidevops status` only warns about it (10 GiB threshold), and that warning did not prevent the disk filling.

## Proposal

1. Add a `docker` row to `aidevops cleanup`: a read-only `docker system df` summary with the owning cleaner.
2. Producer-owned retention for worker-built images. Label images built by workers (for example `sh.aidevops.issue=<N>`, `sh.aidevops.created=<ts>`), then prune labelled images whose issue/PR is terminal or older than N days. Run `docker builder prune --filter until=<window>` under r922.
3. Escalate the npm cache advisory when free disk space is under a threshold (for example <5% free). Keep mutation on the explicit `npm-cache-helper.sh clean --apply --confirm clean-npm-cache` path.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh` (report row and dispatch)
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle.md` (inventory row: Docker images/build cache, external/joint owner)
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-store-policies.md` (policy)
- Worker build paths that call `docker build`: find with `rg -n "docker build" .agents/`

## Verification

- `aidevops cleanup` shows a docker row with sizes, or a visible timeout.
- A dry run lists only labelled worker images and never unlabelled user images or volumes.
- ShellCheck clean.

## Task Brief

## What

Interactive OpenCode sessions stop with a terminal "Overloaded" provider error and never resume. Add a plugin-level session retry that waits about one minute after a terminal provider-overload error and then continues the stopped primary session automatically, with a bounded attempt budget and user-visible toasts.

## Why

OpenCode 1.19.6 already retries overload errors inside a turn, but only briefly: the embedded retry policy uses `zc=2000` (2 s initial), `Hc=2` (doubling), `Xc=30000` (30 s cap without headers) and `Qc=5` (attempt limit). Once those attempts are exhausted the session emits a terminal `session.error` and goes idle, so a provider overload lasting longer than about 60-90 s stops the session until the user types "continue".

Evidence (local runtime events, `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db`, 2026-11-25):

- Three root `claude-opus-5-5` sessions ended at 04:56:52Z, 04:56:54Z and 04:57:12Z with `session.error` → `APIError`, HTTP 529 (`overloaded_error`), `is_retryable: true`, followed by `session.idle`.
- In one of those sessions, ~10 `session.status` busy/retry cycles over ~95 s preceded the terminal error. Nothing resumed the session afterwards.
- The plugin's turn diagnostics toast currently tells the user "Nothing was retried automatically."

## Acceptance

1. A terminal overload `session.error` in a root interactive session schedules exactly one continuation after the configured delay, using the session's last agent/model/variant.
2. User takeover before the delay cancels the retry; a busy live status at fire time skips the prompt.
3. Headless and child sessions are never retried; non-overload errors (403, 400, aborts, context overflow) are never retried.
4. Attempts stop at the cap with a "gave up" toast; a successful reply resets the budget.
5. `AIDEVOPS_OVERLOAD_RETRY=0` disables the feature and restores the existing diagnostics toast.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-overload-retry.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-turn-diagnostics.mjs`
- `node --check` on the changed modules; repository plugin test runner/linters as configured.
- Runtime: deploy via `setup.sh --non-interactive` and confirm the plugin loads (plugin health stage) in a fresh OpenCode session.
